# Classify Attributes (LLM)

The Classify Attributes (LLM) node scores several specialist questions in one cached batched call. Each attribute is its own prompt, the same first-token letter menu as [Classify Intent (LLM)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent-llm.html), and the node writes one slot per attribute. Any attribute whose own rule fires takes `triggered`; otherwise the node takes `default`. `NodeType`: `ClassifyAttributesLLM` (union ordinal 17).

There is no shared-prompt mode. Empty `system_prompt` selects a kind-specific default. Choice and Score templates must reference `{{intents_block}}`. A Boolean template must also reference `{{statement}}`. `history_turns` defaults to 0. `context_size` 0 sizes the window from the rendered prompts. The node forces a unified KV cache and one sequence per attribute plus the dialog sequence. `temperature` 0 means 1.0 for every attribute.

## Parameters

| Param           | Type                       | Default                       | Range      | Structural | Localizable | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------- | ---------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model_name`    | str                        | empty                         | —          | ✓          | —           | Model catalog name. Structural because the token-ID mapping is built from the model's vocabulary at construction.                                                                                                                              |
| `context_size`  | int                        | 0 -> auto                     | ≥ 0.0      | ✓          | —           | KV-cache window in tokens. 0 = size from the rendered specialist prompts plus a per-attribute tail budget, else the classify default.                                                                                                          |
| `attributes`    | list[ClassifyAttributeDef] | empty list                    | —          | —          | —           | The attributes to classify. 1-16 entries, unique names. Shape, name, kind and choice id/prompt are structural; the hand-written Apply allows statement, prompt, decision and trigger edits.                                                    |
| `input`         | str                        | empty                         | —          | ✓          | —           | Slot name this node consumes. Empty = "user_message".                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `history_turns` | int                        | 0                             | 0.0 – 64.0 | —          | —           | Dialog turns included before the current user text. Default 0 until history quality is measured.                                                                                                                                               |
| `temperature`   | float                      | 0.0                           | 0.0 – 8.0  | —          | —           | Softmax temperature for every attribute. 0 = 1.0 (identity).                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `on_failure`    | AttributeFailureRoute      | AttributeFailureRoute.Default | —          | —          | —           | Exit taken when scoring fails.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `notify_client` | NotifyClient               | NotifyClient.Disabled         | —          | —          | —           | When to fire OnNodeEvent("attributes_classified", …). OnFound means the triggered exit was taken.                                                                                                                                              |
| `output_name`   | str                        | empty                         | —          | ✓          | —           | Slot namespace. Empty = node name.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `context`       | ContextOverrides           | unset                         | —          | ✓          | —           | Backend context construction. The node derives n_seq_max and n_outputs_max from the attribute count. Structural.                                                                                                                               |
| `adaptation`    | ModelAdaptation            | unset                         | —          | ✓          | —           | Changes how the model behaves for this node (LoRA adapters; later control vectors). Null = base model. Structural: applied to the llama context at creation, so a change means a new context. Appended last so existing field IDs do not move. |

## Exits

Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

| Exit        | Param field      | Description                                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`   | `default_exit`   | Exit taken when no attribute triggers. Empty string = END.                                                     |
| `triggered` | `triggered_exit` | Exit taken when any attribute triggers, or when on_failure is Triggered and scoring fails. Empty string = END. |

LoRA adapters

`adaptation.loras` runs this node's model with one or more fine-tuned LoRA adapters, each with a scale. See [Use a LoRA Adapter](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-a-lora-adapter.html) for where to put the file and how to tune the scale.

## Kinds

| Kind    | Slot value                                                                                                                       | Trigger                                                                       |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Choice  | Winning choice id. Below `threshold` or `margin`, the slot is `uncertain_choice`: a real choice id, or the reserved `#uncertain` | The written choice's `triggers` flag. `#uncertain` never triggers             |
| Boolean | `"true"` when P(A) ≥ `threshold`, else `"false"`. The menu is fixed: A = True, B = False                                         | `boolean_trigger`: Never, True, or False                                      |
| Score   | Normalised expected level `(Σ i·p_i)/(N−1)`, four decimals in `0.0000`…`1.0000`                                                  | `score_trigger` against `score_threshold` in 0..1: Never, AtOrAbove, or Below |

Choice needs 2–26 options. `uncertain_choice` names one of them, or the reserved `#uncertain`. `#uncertain` is not a letter in the menu. A real id rewrites an uncertain call to that choice and uses its `triggers` flag, including when that choice wins outright. `#uncertain` writes that token and stays on `default`. Boolean takes a `statement` and no choices. Score takes 2–26 levels from low to high; choice `triggers` must stay false. A score of 0.7 means 70% of the way from the lowest level to the highest, not the probability of the top level. Recalibrate any threshold that used to compare a raw level index.

`triggered_exit` must be set exactly when at least one attribute can trigger. Empty input never triggers and takes `default`. If scoring throws or the result shape does not match the attributes, every slot gets its fallback (Choice `uncertain_choice`, Boolean `"false"`, Score `"0.0000"`) and the node follows `on_failure` (`default` or `triggered`). There is no third exit.

## Slots, diagnostics, and the event

Each attribute writes `<output_name>_<name>` (`output_name` empty means the node name). Diagnostics `output.classification` carries `status` (`ok`, `empty_input`, `failed`), `triggered`, and `attributes[]` with `name`, `kind`, `value`, `status`, `triggered`, and `choices[]` of `{id, prob, triggers}`. Choice also reports top and second probability. Boolean reports `p_true` and `p_false`. Score reports `expected_level`, `score`, and entropy `confidence`. Probabilities are measurements, not a contract to pin in a golden file.

`notify_client` `Always` emits `attributes_classified` on every scored turn. `OnFound` emits it only when the triggered exit is taken. The payload is a flat string map: `exit`, `status`, per-attribute kind/value/status/triggered, `prob.<choice_id>`, and `triggered_by`.

Shape, name, kind, and choice id/prompt are structural. Statement, prompt, thresholds, margins, and trigger flags can change after creation.

## Example

```
from tryll_client._generated.node_params import (
    AttributeKind,
    BooleanTrigger,
    ClassifyAttributeChoice,
    ClassifyAttributeDef,
    ClassifyAttributesLLMParams,
    ScoreTrigger,
)
from tryll_client.graph import GraphDescription

graph = GraphDescription()
graph.add_classify_attributes_llm("attrs", ClassifyAttributesLLMParams(
    history_turns=0,
    default_exit="reply",
    triggered_exit="hold",
    attributes=[
        ClassifyAttributeDef(
            name="topic",
            kind=AttributeKind.Choice,
            choices=[
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="world", prompt="ordinary story talk"),
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="meta", prompt="about the software", triggers=True),
            ],
            uncertain_choice="world",
        ),
        ClassifyAttributeDef(
            name="software",
            kind=AttributeKind.Boolean,
            statement="The message is about software or instructions.",
            boolean_trigger=BooleanTrigger.True_,
        ),
        ClassifyAttributeDef(
            name="hostility",
            kind=AttributeKind.Score,
            choices=[
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="calm", prompt="no insult or threat"),
                ClassifyAttributeChoice(id="violent", prompt="a threat of harm"),
            ],
            score_trigger=ScoreTrigger.AtOrAbove,
            score_threshold=0.7,
        ),
    ],
))
```

Graphs authored against the proof-of-concept fields (`independent_prompts`, `choice_ids`, `code_style`, `context.kv_unified`, `context.flash_attn`) do not load. Move each specialist prompt onto the attribute, put `triggers` on the choice that should take `triggered_exit`, and drop the shared-prompt knobs.

## Related

- [How-to: Use a LoRA adapter](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-a-lora-adapter.html)
- [Classify Intent (LLM)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent-llm.html)

# Classify Intent (LLM)

The Classify Intent (LLM) node maps a user message to a discrete **intent label** using a small language model's **first-token logprob** over a closed set of letter candidates (`A`, `B`, `C`, …). Each letter maps positionally to an entry in `intents`. It writes the decision to the slot `output_name` (empty = the node's name), so a [Branch](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/branch.html) can test it. On success it also attaches an `IntentionComponent` — the same routing-only component produced by [Classify Intent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent.html) — so downstream [IntentToInstruction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/intent-to-instruction.html) wiring is unchanged.

`NodeType`: `ClassifyIntentLLM`.

## How it works

1. Projects the dialog via `ClassifyIntentLLMProjectionStrategy`:
1. Stable **system** message — `system_prompt` rendered as a Mustache template against the pre-built label list; see [The system prompt](#the-system-prompt).
1. Up to `history_turns` past **user** / **assistant** pairs for coreference (history turns always replay the `user_message` slot).
1. Current turn's `input`-resolved slot as the **user** message (empty = `user_message`).
1. Prefills the classifier model (`Sync()`); reuses KV-cache prefix across turns when the prompt tail is append-only.
1. Reads logits at the final position and softmaxes over the single-token ids for `A`, `B`, `C`, …
1. If `top_prob ≥ threshold` and `(top − second) ≥ margin`, attaches `IntentionComponent` for the winning id and returns `found`.
1. Writes the output slot on every path — see [Output slot](#output-slot).

No text is generated; no sampling.

## Output slot

The node writes one turn-local slot, `slot.<output_name>`, whichever exit it takes. Empty `output_name` uses the node's own name.

| Exit        | Slot value                                                                                   |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `found`     | The winning intent id.                                                                       |
| `not_found` | `not_found_intent` — an intent id, the reserved `#uncertain`, or an empty string when unset. |

`not_found_intent` is written on every `not_found` reason: `below_threshold`, `below_margin`, `sink_intent`, `empty_message` and scoring failures. This is the same rule as the `uncertain_choice` of a `Choice` attribute on [Classify Attributes (LLM)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-attributes-llm.html). Because the slot is always written, a `Branch` placed after either exit can read it.

## The system prompt

`system_prompt` is a [Mustache](https://mustache.github.io/) template rendered against a context with two variables:

| Variable            | Required | Renders to                                                             |
| ------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{{intents_block}}` | yes      | The label list, one line per intent prompt: `A. <first>\nB. <second>…` |
| `{{letters}}`       | no       | The candidate letters, comma-joined: `A, B, C`                         |

`system_prompt` is required. Empty, unparsable, or missing `{{intents_block}}` (padded and triple-brace forms count) fails `CreateAgent` and `ChangeAgentParam`. `{{letters}}` is still substituted if you write it; leave it out unless you have a reason. There is no built-in default template.

This is **not** the [`Generate`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html) / [`Transform`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/transform.html) Mustache context: `user_message`, `slot.<name>`, `var.<name>`, `instructions` and `knowledge` do not resolve here. The classified text arrives as its own user turn, added by the projection.

A minimal working template:

```
You are an intent classifier. Pick the best label for the user's LATEST message,
using the conversation as context for pronouns and references.

Labels:
{{intents_block}}

Respond with a single letter. No other text.
```

With three `intents` entries whose prompts are "asks the price", "wants to haggle", and "anything else", the model receives:

```
You are an intent classifier. Pick the best label for the user's LATEST message,
using the conversation as context for pronouns and references.

Labels:
A. asks the price
B. wants to haggle
C. anything else

Respond with a single letter. No other text.
```

Intent ids are never rendered — they supply the label attached on a win, for downstream routing only. For what to write in the template and how to order the labels, see [Design an intent-classifier prompt](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/design-an-intent-classifier-prompt.html).

## Context window

Leave `context_size` at `0` to use this node's **2048-token** default (then the model variant, then the server `default_n_ctx`). That is enough for typical classifier prompts with a few history turns and is far cheaper than the 8192 Generate default. The `context` table is an advanced structural override (`kv_cache_type`, veto-only `offload_kqv`, escape-hatch batch sizes). Do not set `q4_0` KV expecting a VRAM win at a right-sized window — measured savings show up only at large `n_ctx` (around 8192).

## Parameters

| Param              | Type                      | Default               | Range      | Structural | Localizable | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ------------------------- | --------------------- | ---------- | ---------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `model_name`       | str                       | empty                 | —          | ✓          | —           | Model catalog name. Structural because the token-ID mapping is built from the model's vocabulary at construction.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `context_size`     | int                       | 0 -> 2048             | ≥ 0.0      | ✓          | —           | KV-cache / context window (n_ctx) for this node in tokens. 0 = node default 2048, else the model variant's context_size, else server default_n_ctx. Validated against the model's trained maximum at agent creation.                                                                                          |
| `system_prompt`    | str (multiline)           | empty                 | —          | —          | ✓           | Mustache template for the classifier's system message. Required: empty or unparsable templates fail agent creation and ChangeAgentParam. Must reference intents_block (the letter-prefixed list built from the resolved prompts). letters (e.g. "A, B, C") is optional — padded and triple-brace forms count. |
| `intents`          | list[ClassifyIntentEntry] | empty list            | —          | ✓          | —           | Intent list: id + prompt pairs. Entry 0 is letter A. 2-26 unique ids, non-empty prompts. Structural because the projection scaffolding and label-token mapping are built at construction.                                                                                                                     |
| `input`            | str                       | empty                 | —          | ✓          | —           | Slot name this node consumes as its primary text for the current turn. Empty = "user_message". Structural: immutable after creation — rebinding would re-wire the slot dataflow that is validated once at agent creation.                                                                                     |
| `output_name`      | str                       | empty                 | —          | ✓          | —           | Name of the slot this node writes on every path. Empty = node name. Holds the winning intent id on found, and not_found_intent (possibly empty) on not_found. Structural: immutable after creation — renaming would re-wire the slot dataflow that is validated once at agent creation.                       |
| `history_turns`    | int                       | 2                     | 0.0 – 64.0 | —          | —           | Number of dialog history turns included in the classification context.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `threshold`        | float                     | 0.5                   | 0.0 – 1.0  | —          | —           | First-token probability threshold for the winning label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `margin`           | float                     | 0.15                  | 0.0 – 1.0  | —          | —           | Minimum margin between top and second label probabilities.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `temperature`      | float                     | 0.0                   | 0.0 – 8.0  | —          | —           | Softmax temperature applied to scored letter probabilities before threshold/margin. 0 = 1.0 (identity). Mutable.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `notify_client`    | NotifyClient              | NotifyClient.Disabled | —          | —          | —           | When to fire OnNodeEvent("intent_llm_classified", …).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `not_found_intent` | str                       | empty                 | —          | —          | —           | Sink intent. When it wins, the node exits not_found. Written to the output slot on every not_found path. One of the intent ids, the reserved "#uncertain", or empty.                                                                                                                                          |
| `context`          | ContextOverrides          | unset                 | —          | ✓          | —           | Backend context construction. Null table inherits, except CreateContext still defaults `n_outputs_max` to 1. Structural.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `adaptation`       | ModelAdaptation           | unset                 | —          | ✓          | —           | Changes how the model behaves for this node (LoRA adapters; later control vectors). Null = base model. Structural: applied to the llama context at creation, so a change means a new context. Appended last so existing field IDs do not move.                                                                |

## Exits

Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

| Exit        | Param field      | Description                                                                                 |
| ----------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `found`     | `found_exit`     | Exit taken when classification produced a label above threshold/margin. Empty string = END. |
| `not_found` | `not_found_exit` | Exit taken when no label cleared the threshold/margin. Empty string = END.                  |

LoRA adapters

`adaptation.loras` runs this node's model with one or more fine-tuned LoRA adapters, each with a scale. See [Use a LoRA Adapter](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-a-lora-adapter.html) for where to put the file and how to tune the scale.

## Exit routes

`temperature` (0 = 1.0, mutable) rescales the scored letter probabilities (`p ← p^(1/T)`) before threshold/margin. Diagnostics emit `parameters.temperature` and, when T ≠ 1, `output.classification.probs_raw`.

| Route       | Fires when                                                                                                             |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `found`     | Valid message, top probability passes `threshold` and `margin`, and winning intent is not the sink.                    |
| `not_found` | Empty message, failed thresholds, internal scoring error, or winning intent equals `not_found_intent` (`sink_intent`). |

`notify_client`: `OnFound` emits `event_type="intent_llm_classified"` on the found path; `Always` also emits on every `not_found` path. KV: `intent`, `top_prob`, `second_prob`, `not_found_reason`, plus one `<label>.prob` per `intents_ids` entry. Subscribe on the agent (`set_on_intent_llm_classified`, `SetOnIntentLlmClassified`, `TryllAgentComponent.IntentLlmClassified`, `UTryllAgentComponent::OnIntentLlmClassified`). Session events are the all-agents form `(agentId, classification)`; the payload has no agent id. A typed subscriber swallows generic `OnNodeEvent` in the same scope only.

## Diagnostics

When `enable_diagnostics = true`, this node contributes to `debug_info.nodes[].diagnostics`. See [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html) for the envelope, the shared `input.prompt[]` shape, and the `engine` counters.

The shared [turn inspector](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-inspector.html#intent) renders this payload as the **Intent** block. Dialog Lab can also assert the accepted label with an **Intent is** / **Intent not found** check — see [Compare dialog variants](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/compare-dialog-variants.html). Raw JSON remains the escape hatch for every field below.

| Key                                      | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                | Absent when                                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parameters.model_name`                  | The model that actually ran, after fallback.                                                                                                                                           | The name could not be resolved.                                                         |
| `parameters.input`                       | The configured input slot name.                                                                                                                                                        | Using the `user_message` default.                                                       |
| `parameters.output_name`                 | The slot this node writes (the node name when `output_name` is empty).                                                                                                                 | —                                                                                       |
| `parameters.threshold`                   | Minimum `top_prob` required to accept a label.                                                                                                                                         | —                                                                                       |
| `parameters.margin`                      | Minimum `top_prob − second_prob` required.                                                                                                                                             | —                                                                                       |
| `parameters.notify_client`               | `Disabled`, `OnFound` or `Always`.                                                                                                                                                     | —                                                                                       |
| `parameters.history_turns`               | How many prior turns were included in the classification prompt.                                                                                                                       | —                                                                                       |
| `parameters.intents_ids[]`               | The label ids **in letter order** — element 0 is `A`, element 1 is `B`, and so on.                                                                                                     | —                                                                                       |
| `input.query`                            | The `input`-resolved text classified. Same string as `output.classification.query` (kept for one release).                                                                             | The resolved text was empty.                                                            |
| `input.prompt[]`                         | The classification prompt as the model received it.                                                                                                                                    | —                                                                                       |
| `output.classification.query`            | The `input`-resolved text classified. Prefer `input.query`.                                                                                                                            | The resolved text was empty.                                                            |
| `output.classification.probs[]`          | Full first-token probability vector. **`probs[i]` is the probability of `parameters.intents_ids[i]`** (letter A = 0). Equal length on `found`; `score_size_mismatch` when they differ. | Scoring did not run.                                                                    |
| `output.classification.top_prob`         | Probability of the winning letter.                                                                                                                                                     | Scoring did not run.                                                                    |
| `output.classification.second_prob`      | Probability of the runner-up letter.                                                                                                                                                   | Scoring did not run.                                                                    |
| `output.classification.margin_result`    | `top_prob − second_prob`, to compare against `parameters.margin`.                                                                                                                      | Scoring did not run.                                                                    |
| `output.classification.predicted_letter` | The winning letter (`A`, `B`, …).                                                                                                                                                      | Nothing was predicted.                                                                  |
| `output.classification.intent`           | The intent label attached.                                                                                                                                                             | The node exited `not_found`.                                                            |
| `output.classification.rejected_intent`  | The label the scorer picked, when routing rejected it.                                                                                                                                 | `found`, or there was no pick (`empty_message`, `score_failed`, `score_size_mismatch`). |
| `output.classification.slot_value`       | The value written to `slot.<output_name>` this turn.                                                                                                                                   | The node has not run.                                                                   |
| `output.classification.not_found_reason` | `empty_message`, `score_size_mismatch`, `score_failed`, `below_threshold`, `below_margin` or `sink_intent`.                                                                            | The node found a match.                                                                 |
| `engine.*`                               | Scheduler counters for the scoring pass — `last_job.kind` is `score`, not `decode`.                                                                                                    | Server config `include_engine_diagnostics` is off.                                      |

To read a `not_found`: `not_found_reason` names the gate that rejected it, and `top_prob` / `margin_result` against `parameters.threshold` / `parameters.margin` show by how much. Pair `probs[]` with `intents_ids[]` positionally to see the full ranking.

## Example

```
from tryll_client.graph import (
    GraphDescription, ClassifyIntentLLMParams, ClassifyIntentEntry, NotifyClient,
)

CLASSIFIER_SYSTEM = (
    "You are an intent classifier for a murder-mystery interrogation.\n"
    "The inspector (user) questions Mr Rixman, the butler (assistant).\n"
    "Pick the single best label for the inspector's LATEST message only.\n\n"
    "Labels:\n{{intents_block}}\n\n"
    "Respond with a single letter. No other text."
)

graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("classify", ClassifyIntentLLMParams(
        model_name="Llama 3.2 1B Instruct (Q4_K_M)",
        intents=[
            ClassifyIntentEntry(id="confess_margaret_saw",
                prompt="inspector confronts butler with Mrs Hollis witness statement"),
            ClassifyIntentEntry(id="when_saw_body",
                prompt="inspector asks when butler first saw the body"),
            ClassifyIntentEntry(id="other", prompt="anything else"),
        ],
        system_prompt=CLASSIFIER_SYSTEM,   # required — must reference intents_block
        history_turns=4,
        threshold=0.5,
        notify_client=NotifyClient.OnFound,
        found_exit="pick_instruction",
        not_found_exit="retrieve_world",
    ))
    # ... rest of graph nodes
    .set_start_node("classify")
    .set_default_model_name("My Local Model")
)
```

```
using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

constexpr const char* kClassifierSystem =
    "You are an intent classifier for a murder-mystery interrogation.\n"
    "The inspector (user) questions Mr Rixman, the butler (assistant).\n"
    "Pick the single best label for the inspector's LATEST message only.\n\n"
    "Labels:\n{{intents_block}}\n\n"
    "Respond with a single letter. No other text.";

ClassifyIntentLLMParamsT cp;
cp.model_name    = "Llama 3.2 1B Instruct (Q4_K_M)";
auto addIntent = [&](const char* id, const char* prompt)
{
    auto e = std::make_unique<ClassifyIntentEntryT>();
    e->id = id;
    e->prompt = prompt;
    cp.intents.push_back(std::move(e));
};
addIntent("confess_margaret_saw",
    "inspector confronts butler with Mrs Hollis witness statement");
addIntent("when_saw_body", "inspector asks when butler first saw the body");
addIntent("other", "anything else");
cp.system_prompt = kClassifierSystem;  // required — must reference intents_block
cp.history_turns  = 4;
cp.threshold      = 0.5f;
cp.notify_client  = Tryll::NotifyClient_OnFound;
cp.found_exit     = "pick_instruction";
cp.not_found_exit = "retrieve_world";

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddClassifyIntentLLM("classify", std::move(cp));
// ... rest of graph nodes
```

## When to use this node

|                    | Classify Intent (embedding)         | Classify Intent (LLM)                |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| **Requires KB**    | Yes — labelled examples needed      | No                                   |
| **Inference cost** | Embedding only (fast)               | One LM forward pass                  |
| **Intent set**     | Fixed at storage creation           | Defined inline as an `intents` array |
| **Best for**       | Large, pre-labelled KB; low latency | Small label sets; no pre-built KB    |

See `tryll_test_chat` agent `butler2` (`IntentLLMWorkflow`) for a full graph alongside retrieval-based `butler`.

# Classify Intent

The Classify Intent node maps a user message to a discrete **intent label** by performing top-1 vector similarity search over a small, labelled [embedded string storage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/embedded-string-storage.html). When a label is found it attaches an `IntentionComponent` to the current [interaction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#interaction) so a downstream [IntentToInstruction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/intent-to-instruction.html) node can branch the graph or look up a matching instruction. A `filter` that does not compile, changed via `ChangeAgentParam`, returns `3007 InvalidParamValue` and leaves the previous filter in force.

It does **not** generate text and does **not** render anything into the prompt — the `IntentionComponent` is routing-only; it is consumed by `IntentToInstructionNode` and not by `DefaultProjectionStrategy`.

`NodeType`: `ClassifyIntent`.

## How it works

1. Reads the `input`-resolved slot (empty = the `user_message` slot).
1. Embeds it with the embedding model recorded in the KB config file.
1. Calls `Search(queryVector, topK=1, predicate)` on the storage — using the same compiled-filter pipeline as [Retrieve](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve.html).
1. If the top hit's cosine distance is ≤ `threshold`, reads the configured `metadata_field` from that record's typed metadata.
1. Attaches `IntentionComponent{intentLabel}` to the interaction and returns `found`. Otherwise returns `not_found`.

The knowledge base records must carry a **string-typed** metadata field whose value is the intent label. See [KB schema requirements](#kb-schema-requirements).

## Parameters

| Param                     | Type         | Default               | Range      | Structural | Localizable | Description                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------ | --------------------- | ---------- | ---------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `embedded_string_storage` | str          | empty                 | —          | ✓          | —           | Named embedded string storage. Structural.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `input`                   | str          | empty                 | —          | ✓          | —           | Slot name this node embeds and searches with. Empty = "user_message". Structural: immutable after creation — rebinding would re-wire the slot dataflow that is validated once at agent creation. |
| `metadata_field`          | str          | empty                 | —          | —          | —           | Storage metadata field whose string value becomes the intent label.                                                                                                                              |
| `threshold`               | float        | 0.25                  | 0.0 – 2.0  | —          | —           | Maximum cosine distance; hits above this are treated as not_found. Cosine distance on normalized vectors is in [0, 2].                                                                           |
| `filter`                  | str          | empty                 | —          | —          | —           | JSON filter applied during search. Empty = no filter. Mutable.                                                                                                                                   |
| `notify_client`           | NotifyClient | NotifyClient.Disabled | —          | —          | —           | When to fire OnNodeEvent("intent_classified", …).                                                                                                                                                |
| `diagnostic_topk`         | int          | 5                     | 1.0 – 64.0 | —          | —           | Hits to fetch for diagnostic purposes (routing always uses top-1).                                                                                                                               |

## Exits

Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

| Exit        | Param field      | Description                                                                            |
| ----------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `found`     | `found_exit`     | Exit taken when the top-1 hit's distance is at or below threshold. Empty string = END. |
| `not_found` | `not_found_exit` | Exit taken when no label cleared the threshold. Empty string = END.                    |

## Exit routes

| Route       | Fires when                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `found`     | Top-1 hit's cosine distance is less than or equal to `threshold` and its `metadata_field` contained a non-empty string. `IntentionComponent` is attached.                |
| `not_found` | Resolved `input` slot missing/empty, empty storage, top-1 distance above `threshold`, or matched record's `metadata_field` is absent or empty. No component is attached. |

An empty exit field routes to END and is valid. A non-empty exit that does not name a node in the graph fails agent creation with [`3003 GraphCompilationFailed`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent).

## Side effects

- Embeds the `input`-resolved text (empty = `user_message`) using the embedding model recorded in the KB config file referenced by `embedded_string_storage`.
- Attaches an `IntentionComponent{intentLabel}` to the current interaction on `found`. The component is **not** rendered into the prompt by `DefaultProjectionStrategy` — it is consumed only by `IntentToInstructionNode`.
- On `not_found`, nothing is attached (a warning is logged if the top hit was rejected for a metadata reason rather than a distance reason).
- When `notify_client` is `OnFound` or `Always`, fires one `NodeEvent` (`event_type="intent_classified"`) out-of-band before the turn completes. `OnFound` emits only on the `found` path; `Always` also emits on every `not_found` path (`empty_message`, `no_results`, `below_threshold`) with `not_found_reason` set and the rejected top-1 fields when a hit exists. Subscribe on the agent: `agent.set_on_intent_classified(cb)` (Python), `agent.SetOnIntentClassified(cb)` (C++), `TryllAgentComponent.IntentClassified` (Unity), or `UTryllAgentComponent::OnIntentClassified` (Unreal). The session events (`TryllClient.IntentClassified`, `UTryllSubsystem::OnIntentClassified`) are the all-agents form `(agentId, classification)`. The payload has no agent id. A typed subscriber swallows the generic `OnNodeEvent` fallback in the same scope only.

## KB schema requirements

The storage's `*.json` config must declare a `fields` array with at least one entry whose `type` is `"string"` — this is the field you reference in the `metadata_field` parameter:

```
{
  "version": 1,
  "embedding_model": "All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
  "records_file": "my_intents.kb.json",
  "index_file":   "my_intents.usearch",
  "fields": [
    { "name": "intent", "type": "string", "default": "" }
  ]
}
```

Each record in `my_intents.kb.json` carries the label in that field:

```
[
  { "id": "ex1", "text": "Move aside, you fool.", "metadata": { "intent": "insult" } },
  { "id": "ex2", "text": "May I please pass through?", "metadata": { "intent": "pleasing" } }
]
```

## Diagnostics

When `enable_diagnostics = true`, this node contributes to `debug_info.nodes[].diagnostics`. See [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html) for the envelope.

The shared [turn inspector](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-inspector.html#intent) renders this payload as the **Intent** block. Dialog Lab can also assert the accepted label with an **Intent is** / **Intent not found** check — see [Compare dialog variants](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/compare-dialog-variants.html). Raw JSON remains the escape hatch for every field below.

| Key                                       | Meaning                                                                                                                                               | Absent when                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `parameters.embedded_string_storage`      | The knowledge base searched.                                                                                                                          | —                                                              |
| `parameters.input`                        | The configured input slot name.                                                                                                                       | Using the `user_message` default.                              |
| `parameters.metadata_field`               | The metadata field read off the winning record to produce the label.                                                                                  | —                                                              |
| `parameters.threshold`                    | Max cosine distance accepted, as a number.                                                                                                            | —                                                              |
| `parameters.notify_client`                | `Disabled`, `OnFound` or `Always`.                                                                                                                    | —                                                              |
| `parameters.diagnostic_topk`              | How many ranked candidates to record below.                                                                                                           | —                                                              |
| `parameters.filter`                       | The active filter, as JSON. Empty string when none.                                                                                                   | —                                                              |
| `input.query`                             | The `input`-resolved text that was embedded.                                                                                                          | The resolved text was empty.                                   |
| `output.classification.topk[]`            | Ranked candidates: `rank` (**0-based**), `intent`, `distance`. Several entries can share one intent when a KB has multiple example phrases per label. | `diagnostic_topk` is 0, or nothing was retrieved.              |
| `output.classification.winner`            | The match that was attached: `intent`, `id`, `text`, `index` (0-based record index), `distance`.                                                      | The node exited `not_found`.                                   |
| `output.classification.rejected_intent`   | The top-1 label the search picked, when routing rejected it.                                                                                          | `found`, or there was no pick (`empty_message`, `no_results`). |
| `output.classification.rejected_distance` | That hit's raw distance.                                                                                                                              | Same as `rejected_intent`.                                     |
| `output.classification.runner_up`         | The best *different* intent: `intent`, `distance`, `margin` (its distance minus the winner's).                                                        | There was no second distinct intent.                           |
| `output.classification.not_found_reason`  | Why `not_found` fired.                                                                                                                                | The node found a match, or recorded no reason.                 |

`runner_up.margin` is the number to watch when a classifier is unstable: a margin near zero means the two labels were nearly tied, and small rewordings will flip the route.

`notify_client` does not gate this block

`notify_client` decides whether the *client* receives an `intent_classified` event. A classification missing from the Agent Log is still recorded here in full.

## Minimum working example

```
from tryll_client.graph import (
    GraphDescription, ClassifyIntentParams, IntentToInstructionParams,
    TransformParams, GenerateParams,
)

# 1. Create intent KB (file-backed, Path A)
client.create_embedded_string_storage(
    name="intent_kb",
    config_path="data/intents/intents.json",
)

# 2. Create instruction map (Map kind)
client.create_keyed_string_storage(
    name="intent_instructions",
    keys=["insult", "pleasing"],
    values=[
        "The user insulted you — respond curtly.",
        "The user is being polite — acknowledge grudgingly.",
    ],
)

# 3. Build the graph
graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("classify", ClassifyIntentParams(
        embedded_string_storage="guard_intents/guard_intents.json",
        metadata_field="intent",
        threshold=0.6,
        found_exit="pick",
        not_found_exit="respond",
    ))
    .add_node("pick", IntentToInstructionParams(
        string_storage="intent_instructions",
        output_name="tone",
        default_exit="compose",
    ))
    .add_node("compose", TransformParams(
        template="{{#instructions}}[{{text}}]\n{{/instructions}}{{user_message}}",
        default_exit="respond",
    ))
    .add_node("respond", GenerateParams(
        input="compose",
        default_exit="",   # empty = END
    ))
    .set_start_node("classify")
    .set_default_model_name("My Local Model")
)

agent = client.create_agent(graph)
```

```
using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

ClassifyIntentParamsT cp;
cp.embedded_string_storage = "guard_intents/guard_intents.json";
cp.metadata_field          = "intent";
cp.threshold               = 0.6f;
cp.found_exit              = "pick";
cp.not_found_exit          = "respond";

IntentToInstructionParamsT pp;
pp.string_storage = "intent_instructions";
pp.output_name    = "tone";
pp.default_exit   = "compose";

TransformParamsT tp;
tp.template_    = "{{#instructions}}[{{text}}]\n{{/instructions}}{{user_message}}";
tp.default_exit = "respond";

GenerateParamsT gp;
gp.input = "compose";
// gp.default_exit = ""; // empty = END (the default)

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddClassifyIntent("classify", std::move(cp))
     .AddIntentToInstruction("pick",     std::move(pp))
     .AddTransform("compose",            std::move(tp))
     .AddGenerate("respond",             std::move(gp))
     .SetStartNode("classify")
     .SetDefaultModelName("My Local Model");

auto agent = client.CreateAgent(graph);
```

```
using Tryll.Client;

var graph = new TryllGraphBuilder()
    .AddClassifyIntent("classify", new TryllClassifyIntentParams
    {
        EmbeddedStringStorage = "guard_intents/guard_intents.json",
        MetadataField         = "intent",
        Threshold             = 0.6f,
        FoundExit             = "pick",
        NotFoundExit          = "respond",
    })
    .AddIntentToInstruction("pick", new TryllIntentToInstructionParams
    {
        StringStorage = "intent_instructions",
        OutputName    = "tone",
        DefaultExit   = "compose",
    })
    .AddTransform("compose", new TryllTransformParams
    {
        Template    = "{{#instructions}}[{{text}}]\n{{/instructions}}{{user_message}}",
        DefaultExit = "respond",
    })
    .AddGenerate("respond", new TryllGenerateParams
    {
        Input = "compose",
    })
    .SetStartNode("classify")
    .SetDefaultModelName("My Local Model")
    .Build();
```

```
#include "Generated/TryllGraphBuilder.Nodes.h"
#include "Generated/TryllNodeParamsFactory.h"

UTryllClassifyIntentParams* CP = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeClassifyIntentParams(this);
CP->bOverrideEmbeddedStringStorage = true;
CP->EmbeddedStringStorage = TEXT("guard_intents/guard_intents.json");
CP->bOverrideMetadataField = true;
CP->MetadataField = TEXT("intent");
CP->Threshold  = 0.6f;
CP->FoundExit    = TEXT("pick");
CP->NotFoundExit = TEXT("respond");

UTryllIntentToInstructionParams* PP = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeIntentToInstructionParams(this);
PP->bOverrideStringStorage = true;
PP->StringStorage = TEXT("intent_instructions");
PP->bOverrideOutputName = true;
PP->OutputName    = TEXT("tone");
PP->DefaultExit   = TEXT("compose");

UTryllTransformParams* TP = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeTransformParams(this);
TP->bOverrideTemplate = true;
TP->Template    = TEXT("{{#instructions}}[{{text}}]\n{{/instructions}}{{user_message}}");
TP->DefaultExit = TEXT("respond");

UTryllGenerateParams* GP = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeGenerateParams(this);
GP->bOverrideInput = true;
GP->Input = TEXT("compose");

FTryllGraphDescription Graph = FTryllGraphBuilder()
    .AddNode(TEXT("classify"), CP)
    .AddNode(TEXT("pick"),     PP)
    .AddNode(TEXT("compose"),  TP)
    .AddNode(TEXT("respond"),  GP)
    .SetStartNode(TEXT("classify"))
    .SetDefaultModelName(TEXT("My Local Model"))
    .Build();
```

- [Glossary](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#classify-intent-node)

# Generate and Speak

The Generate-and-Speak node fuses LLM token generation with streaming [TTS](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#tts) synthesis: it runs the same projection and [language-model](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#language-model) inference as a [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html) node, but as tokens arrive it segments them into sentences, dispatches each sentence to a dedicated TTS strand, and emits PCM audio frames alongside the text deltas.

Because synthesis overlaps generation, audio begins after roughly the first sentence (`min_sentence_chars`) rather than after the whole answer — the TTS of one sentence runs while the LLM is still generating the next. This is the lowest-latency way to speak a generated answer (measured by the `time_to_first_audio_ms` diagnostic). `sampling.max_tokens` is fixed at creation, the same as on [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html). Chaining a standalone [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html) → [Speak](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/speak.html) instead (with Speak's `input` set to the Generate node's output) produces the same voice but cannot start until generation has fully finished, since `Speak` only sees the completed text. Prefer this fused node when you want a generated answer spoken with minimal delay, and the split form only when you need to branch on, inspect, or transform the text in between.

The node has no voice settings. It speaks with the agent's [voice profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html), which you pass when you create the agent. A graph with a Generate and Speak node and no voice fails agent creation with `3025 AgentVoiceRequired`. The TTS model, speaker, speed, language, reference clip, delivery mode and `emit_visemes` all come from the profile. The node keeps its language-model settings and its chunking (`min_sentence_chars`, `first_chunk_max_chars`).

The audio format is announced once per turn, by the first speaking node that produces audio, so a later [Speak](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/speak.html) node in the same turn reuses it. With the voice's `emit_visemes` on, the node sends one lip-sync viseme frame per sentence.

`NodeType`: `GenerateAndSpeak`.

Leave `context_size` at `0` to inherit the model variant's window, then the server `default_n_ctx` (commonly 8192) — the same resolution as [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html). The `context` table is an advanced structural override. Do not set `q4_0` KV expecting a VRAM win at a right-sized window.

Neither cut fires before 5 words or min_sentence_chars. Later chunks keep whole sentences. ## Exits

Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

| Exit      | Param field    | Description                                                                                  |
| --------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | `default_exit` | Default exit target — routes here after generation + synthesis complete. Empty string = END. |

LoRA adapters

`adaptation.loras` runs this node's model with one or more fine-tuned LoRA adapters, each with a scale. See [Use a LoRA Adapter](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-a-lora-adapter.html) for where to put the file and how to tune the scale.

## Constrained output (GBNF grammar)

Like [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html#constrained-output-gbnf-grammar), this node accepts an optional `grammar` (GBNF) that constrains the generated output at every decode step. The full rules there apply verbatim (must contain a `root` rule; fail-fast at agent creation and `InvalidParamValue` 3007 on a bad mutation; mutable per turn; constrain the wire, not the thinking).

The fit here is **narrower** than on Generate: the constrained output is also *spoken*, so grammar only makes sense when the constrained text is itself meant to be voiced — e.g. restricting an NPC to a fixed set of barks or canned lines:

```
root ::= "Halt!" | "Who goes there?" | "Move along." | "For the throne!"
```

Note the interaction with `min_sentence_chars` (default 12): very short constrained output may never cross the sentence-boundary threshold, so the whole (tiny) output flushes as a single TTS call — which is fine for barks.

See [Concept: Constrained output (GBNF)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/constrained-output.html) for what a grammar does and doesn't guarantee, and [How to constrain output with a grammar](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/constrain-output-with-a-grammar.html) for a worked example.

## Diagnostics

When `enable_diagnostics = true`, this node contributes to `debug_info.nodes[].diagnostics`. See [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html) for the envelope, the shared `input.prompt[]` shape, and the `engine` counters.

This is the only node that emits a fifth section, **`tts`** — the voice half of the fused step is kept separate from the language-model parameters. It holds the agent's [voice](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html#diagnostics) as it was when the node ran, plus this node's chunking.

# Instruction Node

**`NodeType = Instruction` (`NodeParams` union discriminator 6)**

Attaches a named instruction string to the current interaction as a [slot](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/slots-and-inter-node-value-passing.html). A downstream `Generate` node can reference it inside a [Mustache template](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-mustache-templates.html) via the `{{#instructions}}` list or the `{{slot.<name>}}` direct lookup.

The node itself does **not** call a model and does **not** modify the conversation history that the model sees. It only adds a `kind=Instruction` `SlotComponent` to the current turn's interaction data, which the projection stage picks up when rendering the Generate node's template.

______________________________________________________________________

## Parameters

| Param         | Type            | Default | Range | Structural | Localizable | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | --------------- | ------- | ----- | ---------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `instruction` | str (multiline) | empty   | —     | —          | ✓           | The instruction text. Mutable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `output_name` | str             | empty   | —     | ✓          | —           | Name this node's output slot is stored under. Empty = the node's own name. Downstream templates look it up via slot.. Structural: immutable after creation — renaming would re-wire the slot dataflow that is validated once at agent creation. |

## Exits

Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

| Exit      | Param field    | Description                                                              |
| --------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `default` | `default_exit` | Default exit target after attaching the instruction. Empty string = END. |

______________________________________________________________________

## Exit routes

| Exit      | Condition                                       |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | Always taken after the instruction is attached. |

______________________________________________________________________

## Mustache exposure

Given a node named `greeter` with `instruction = "Welcome the user."`:

| Template expression                                    | Renders to                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------- |
| `{{slot.greeter}}`                                     | `Welcome the user.`          |
| `{{#instructions}}{{name}}: {{text}}{{/instructions}}` | `greeter: Welcome the user.` |

Multiple `Instruction` nodes in one graph each contribute one entry to the `{{#instructions}}` list, in the order they executed.

______________________________________________________________________

## Diagnostics

When `enable_diagnostics = true`, this node contributes to `debug_info.nodes[].diagnostics`. See [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html) for the envelope.

Instruction records a single key, and no `input`, `output` or `engine` section.

| Key                      | Meaning                                         | Absent when |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `parameters.instruction` | The static instruction text this node injected. | —           |

Whether that instruction reached the model is a separate question, answered by the downstream Generate node's `input.prompt[]` — an `Instruction` node that ran is not proof its text was rendered, since that depends on the consuming node's `template`.

______________________________________________________________________

## Example

```
from copy import deepcopy
from tryll_client.graph import GraphDescription, InstructionParams, GenerateParams, Placement

greeter_baseline = InstructionParams(
    instruction="You are a friendly greeter. Welcome the user warmly.",
    default_exit="generate",
)

graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("greeter", greeter_baseline)
    .add_node("generate", GenerateParams(
        template="{{slot.greeter}}",
        placement=Placement.BeforeUserAsSystem,
        default_exit="",   # empty = END
    ))
    .set_start_node("greeter")
    .set_default_model_name("Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)")
)
agent = client.create_agent(graph)

# Change the instruction without recreating the agent:
p = deepcopy(greeter_baseline)
p.instruction = "You are a stern librarian."
agent.change_params("greeter", p)
```

```
using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

InstructionParamsT ip;
ip.instruction  = "You are a friendly greeter. Welcome the user warmly.";
ip.default_exit = "generate";
InstructionParamsT greeterBaseline = ip; // keep a copy for mutations

GenerateParamsT gp;
gp.template_  = "{{slot.greeter}}";
gp.placement  = ::Tryll::Placement_BeforeUserAsSystem;
// gp.default_exit = ""; // empty = END (the default)

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddInstruction("greeter",   std::move(ip))
     .AddGenerate("generate",     std::move(gp))
     .SetStartNode("greeter")
     .SetDefaultModelName("Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)");
auto agent = client.CreateAgent(graph);

// Change the instruction without recreating the agent:
InstructionParamsT mutated = greeterBaseline;
mutated.instruction = "You are a stern librarian.";
agent.ChangeParams("greeter", std::move(mutated));
```

# Intent to Instruction

The Intent to Instruction node looks up the **intent label** written by a preceding [ClassifyIntent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent.html) node in a [`Map`-kind string storage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/string-storage.html), and attaches the matching value as a `kind=Instruction` [slot](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/slots-and-inter-node-value-passing.html) to the current [interaction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#interaction). Changing `string_storage` to a name that cannot be loaded, or to empty, returns `3007 InvalidParamValue` and leaves the previous map in force.

The attached instruction is then rendered into the prompt by the downstream [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html) node's [Mustache template](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-mustache-templates.html) via the `{{#instructions}}` loop or the `{{slot.<name>}}` direct lookup.

`NodeType`: `IntentToInstruction`.

## How it works

1. Reads `IntentionComponent` from the current interaction (written by an upstream `ClassifyIntent` node).
1. Calls `FindFirst(intentLabel)` on the configured `Map` string storage.
1. If a match is found, attaches `SlotComponent{outputName, matchedText, SlotKind::Instruction, ...}` and returns `"default"`.
1. If no `IntentionComponent` is present, or the key is not found in the map, logs a warning and returns `"default"` without attaching any component. The downstream `Generate` node's template renders the instructions loop as empty, producing a general answer.

The node **always** takes the `"default"` exit — it never blocks or branches. Missing intents and missing keys are handled silently (with a log warning) so the graph keeps running without hard failures.

## Parameters

| Param            | Type                  | Default    | Range | Structural | Localizable | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | --------------------- | ---------- | ----- | ---------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `string_storage` | str                   | empty      | —     | —          | —           | Named session Map-kind string storage. Mutable — rebinds the storage.                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `inline_keys`    | list[str]             | empty list | —     | ✓          | —           | Inline map keys (equal-length with inline_strings). Structural because they materialise the in-memory Map storage at construction.                                                                                                              |
| `inline_strings` | list[str] (multiline) | empty list | —     | ✓          | —           | Inline map values (equal-length with inline_keys). Structural.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `output_name`    | str                   | empty      | —     | ✓          | —           | Name this node's output slot is stored under. Empty = the node's own name. Downstream templates look it up via slot.. Structural: immutable after creation — renaming would re-wire the slot dataflow that is validated once at agent creation. |

## Exits

Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

| Exit      | Param field    | Description                                                                        |
| --------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | `default_exit` | Default exit target after mapping an intent to an instruction. Empty string = END. |

## Exit routes

| Route     | Fires when                                                                                                                                  |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | Always — the node never branches. Set `default_exit` to the downstream `Generate` node name, or leave it empty to terminate the turn (END). |

The `"default"` exit fires regardless of whether an instruction was found. When nothing is found the template's `{{#instructions}}` loop renders as empty.

## Side effects

- Attaches a `kind=Instruction` `SlotComponent{name=outputName, text}` to the current interaction when a matching key is found. The slot is rendered into the prompt by the downstream `GenerateNode` via:
  - `{{#instructions}}{{text}}{{/instructions}}` — iterates all attached instruction-kind slots.
  - `{{slot.<name>}}` — renders only the slot with the matching name.
- When no instruction is attached (missing `IntentionComponent` or missing key), `{{#instructions}}` renders as empty and the model produces a general response.

## Diagnostics

When `enable_diagnostics = true`, this node contributes to `debug_info.nodes[].diagnostics`. See [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html) for the envelope.

No model runs, so the node emits `parameters` and `output` only.

| Key                         | Meaning                                                       | Absent when                       |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `parameters.string_storage` | Name of the `Map`-kind storage that was looked up.            | —                                 |
| `parameters.output_name`    | Name given to the emitted component.                          | —                                 |
| `output.intent`             | The intent label read from the turn's `IntentionComponent`.   | No classification node wrote one. |
| `output.found`              | `true` when the key matched and the instruction was attached. | —                                 |
| `output.text`               | The instruction text that was attached.                       | `found` is `false`.               |

`found: false` with a non-empty `output.intent` means the classifier produced a label the map has no entry for — a KB gap. An **absent** `output.intent` means no classification reached this node at all, which is an upstream routing problem instead. Check the classifier's own `output.classification` in the same payload.

## Minimum working example

```
from tryll_client.graph import (
    GraphDescription, ClassifyIntentParams, IntentToInstructionParams,
    TransformParams, GenerateParams,
)

# Create a Map storage: key = intent label, value = instruction text
client.create_keyed_string_storage(
    name="npc_instructions",
    keys=["insult", "pleasing", "joking"],
    values=[
        "The user insulted you. Respond curtly and insult them back.",
        "The user is being polite. Show grudging satisfaction.",
        'The user told a joke. Laugh once ("Ha."), then refocus on duty.',
    ],
)

# The IntentToInstruction node is wired after a ClassifyIntent node
graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("classify", ClassifyIntentParams(
        embedded_string_storage="intent_kb",
        embedding_model="All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
        metadata_field="intent",
        threshold=0.6,
        found_exit="pick",
        not_found_exit="respond",
    ))
    .add_node("pick", IntentToInstructionParams(
        string_storage="npc_instructions",
        output_name="tone",
        default_exit="compose",
    ))
    .add_node("compose", TransformParams(
        template="{{#instructions}}[Tone: {{text}}]\n{{/instructions}}{{user_message}}",
        default_exit="respond",
    ))
    .add_node("respond", GenerateParams(
        input="compose",
        default_exit="",   # empty = END
    ))
    .set_start_node("classify")
    .set_default_model_name("My Local Model")
)

agent = client.create_agent(graph)
```

```
using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

ClassifyIntentParamsT cp;
cp.embedded_string_storage = "intent_kb";
cp.embedding_model         = "All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)";
cp.metadata_field          = "intent";
cp.threshold               = 0.6f;
cp.found_exit              = "pick";
cp.not_found_exit          = "respond";

IntentToInstructionParamsT pp;
pp.string_storage = "npc_instructions";
pp.output_name    = "tone";
pp.default_exit   = "compose";

TransformParamsT tp;
tp.template_    = "{{#instructions}}[Tone: {{text}}]\n{{/instructions}}{{user_message}}";
tp.default_exit = "respond";

GenerateParamsT gp;
gp.input = "compose";
// gp.default_exit = ""; // empty = END (the default)

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddClassifyIntent("classify", std::move(cp))
     .AddIntentToInstruction("pick",     std::move(pp))
     .AddTransform("compose",            std::move(tp))
     .AddGenerate("respond",             std::move(gp))
     .SetStartNode("classify")
     .SetDefaultModelName("My Local Model");

auto agent = client.CreateAgent(graph);
```

