# WriteToMemory Node

**`NodeType = WriteToMemory` (`NodeParams` union discriminator 15)**

Experimental mutable-KB write. Upserts the current input slot into a session-scoped named store. Place a Retrieve on the same store **before** this node in the same turn if the model should see prior memory — a write does not refresh already-projected knowledge.

An empty input writes nothing and takes `written`. Only a rejected write (overflow, schema mismatch, missing store) takes `failed`.

## Parameters

| Param          | Type | Default | Range | Structural | Localizable | Description                                                                                                                |
| -------------- | ---- | ------- | ----- | ---------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `storage_name` | str  | empty   | —     | ✓          | —           | Session-scoped store name. May contain var.\* templates resolved at agent creation. Structural.                            |
| `schema`       | str  | empty   | —     | ✓          | —           | Catalog schema name. Structural.                                                                                           |
| `input`        | str  | empty   | —     | ✓          | —           | Slot whose text is written. Empty = "user_message".                                                                        |
| `id`           | str  | empty   | —     | —          | —           | Record id, optionally templated with var.\* and resolved per turn. Empty asks the store to assign an insertion-ordered id. |

## Exits

Each exit is a structural string field on the node's params; its value names the target node (empty = END).

| Exit      | Param field    | Description                                                        |
| --------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `written` | `written_exit` | Exit taken after a successful write or a no-op empty input.        |
| `failed`  | `failed_exit`  | Exit taken when the write is rejected (overflow, schema mismatch). |

## Schema picker (Unity)

`schema` is picked from the bundled `data/schemas.json` catalog (same `[TryllSchema]` drawer as Retrieve). `(none)` is offered; unknown values stay visible as **Unregistered**. Server validation is authoritative.

## Exit routes

| Exit      | Condition                                                   |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `written` | The upsert was accepted, or the input was empty (no-op).    |
| `failed`  | The upsert was rejected or the per-turn id template failed. |

## First-use cost

The first write to a new store embeds the record inline. Loading a GameMemory snapshot with `embed_timing=Now` batch-embeds every imported store before the response; `Lazy` installs text immediately and embeds on the first dense or hybrid search.
# Reference

# Reference

Complete, declarative documentation of every Tryll surface. Use this section when you need an authoritative answer about what a field is, what values it accepts, or what a specific error code means. For conceptual background, see the [Concepts](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/index.html) section; for task-driven walkthroughs, see [How-to](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/index.html).

It splits in two: **[Client API](#client-api)** is what your game code calls, **[Workflows and data](#workflows-and-data)** is what you declare for the server to execute.

## Client API

The surface your game code touches — one page per platform, plus the request fields, diagnostics, and errors shared by all of them.

### Per platform

- [Unity](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/index.html) — the `com.tryll.client` package: `TryllClient`, `TryllAgentComponent`, `TryllWorkflowAsset`, `TryllRuntimeSettings`, `TryllSpeaker`, `TryllVoiceInputComponent`.
- [Unreal C++](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unreal/cpp/index.html) — `TryllClient` plugin headers: `UTryllSubsystem`, `FTryllAgent`, and friends.
- [Unreal Blueprint](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unreal/blueprint-catalog.html) — every Blueprint-exposed UFUNCTION.
- [C++](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/cpp/index.html) — `Tryll::Client::*`.
- [Python](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/python/index.html) — `tryll_client`.

### Shared across platforms

- [Agent Parameters](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/agent-parameters.html) — every field on `CreateAgentRequest`: graph, default model name, diagnostics, dialogue-history retention, variables, KV-cache initialization, workload. Tool schemas live on the [Tool Call](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/tool-call.html) node, not on the request.
- [Turn Inspector](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-inspector.html) — the shared per-turn diagnostics panel: every block, when each appears, and what to do when one is missing. Hosted by the Chat Window, Agent Log, and Dialog Lab.
- [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html) — every field of the `debug_info` payload behind that panel, and behind `TurnComplete` on the wire: the envelope, the per-node sections, and why a key is absent.
- [Error Codes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html) — numeric catalog, ranges, per-code recovery guidance.

## Workflows and data

What you declare, and what the server does with it.

### Workflow nodes

[Node catalog](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/index.html) — the table of every node type, its exits, and whether it needs a model. Start there when choosing a node.

| Node                                                                                                  | What it does                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html)                           | Run a language model on the projected dialogue and emit its answer.           |
| [Generate and Speak](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate-and-speak.html)       | Generate and synthesize speech in one fused streaming step.                   |
| [Speak](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/speak.html)                                 | TTS-only — voice text another node already produced.                          |
| [Instruction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/instruction.html)                     | Inject a static instruction via the `{{#instructions}}` block.                |
| [Transform](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/transform.html)                         | Model-free Mustache rendering into a slot; emits nothing on the wire.         |
| [Branch](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/branch.html)                               | Model-free conditional routing on a slot or agent variable.                   |
| [Pause](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/pause.html)                                 | Suspend the turn between nodes and hand control back to the client.           |
| [Retrieve](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve.html)                           | Search an embedded string storage and attach the hits as knowledge.           |
| [Write to Memory](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/write-to-memory.html)             | Experimental: upsert a record into a named mutable knowledge base.            |
| [Summarize](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/summarize.html)                         | Fold ageing turns into a rolling summary so long conversations stay coherent. |
| [Classify Intent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent.html)             | Label the input by top-1 embedding similarity; exits `found` / `not_found`.   |
| [Classify Intent (LLM)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent-llm.html)   | Label the input by first-token logprob on a small model.                      |
| [Intent to Instruction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/intent-to-instruction.html) | Map an intent label to an instruction through a `Map`-kind storage.           |
| [Tool Call](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/tool-call.html)                         | Advertise tools, let the model call them, control notify/pause/results.       |
| [Canned Response](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/canned-response.html)             | Emit a fixed reply from a string storage — no model involved.                 |
| [Regex Guardrail](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/regex-guardrail.html)             | Match input against patterns and route away before spending a model call.     |

[Filter grammar](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve-filter-grammar.html) is not a node: it is the JSON predicate language that Retrieve and Classify Intent accept in their `filter` param for metadata-filtered search.

[Voice Profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html) is not a node either: it is the agent's one voice, which every Speak and Generate and Speak node of the agent uses. It holds the TTS model, the voice identity, and the named delivery modes.

### Knowledge and strings

- [String Storage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/string-storage.html) — session-owned name-to-strings containers (`List` / `Map` / `Multimap`) used by canned-response, guardrail, and intent nodes.
- [Embedded String Storage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/embedded-string-storage.html) — vector-indexed knowledge bases used by retrieve and intent nodes.

### Models

- [Model Management](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/model-management.html) — `models.json` schema, variants, download and load lifecycle, model status.
- [TTS Models](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/tts-models.html) — shipped voices (Sherpa-ONNX and llama.cpp SNAC), which families Tryll supports, and why the rest cannot load.

### Server

- [Server Configuration](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/server-configuration.html) — every field of `server-config.json`.
- [Telemetry](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/telemetry.html) — what usage telemetry collects, and how to turn it off.
- [Wire Protocol](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html) — TCP framing, FlatBuffers schema, session flow, `ErrorResponse` shape. The contract a third-party client must implement.

## Glossary

- [Glossary](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html) — canonical definitions for every term used across the documentation. Check here before guessing what a word means.

# Glossary

Canonical definitions for every term used across the Tryll documentation. Every page links the **first mention** of a term below to its anchor on this page. Subsequent mentions render as plain text.

Terms are grouped by topic so related concepts sit next to each other.

______________________________________________________________________

## Sessions, agents, and turns

### Agent

A server-side object that owns one conversation: its [dialog](#dialog), its compiled [workflow](#workflow), its retained knowledge, and a handle to the [models](#language-model) it needs. Each agent belongs to exactly one [session](#session) and is referenced by a numeric `agent_id`. Created via `CreateAgentRequest`, retired via `DestroyAgentRequest`.

### Session

A single configured connection between a client and the Tryll server. The client opens a TCP socket, sends a `CreateSessionRequest`, and receives a `session_id`. All subsequent requests from that socket are scoped to the session; closing the socket ends the session and destroys every [agent](#agent) it owns.

### Turn

One request–response cycle initiated by a user message. A turn begins when the client sends `SendMessageRequest` and ends when the server emits `TurnComplete`. Between those two frames the client may receive zero or more `AnswerText` chunks (see [streaming](#streaming)). Only one turn is in flight per agent at a time.

### Dialog

The ordered list of interactions belonging to an [agent](#agent) — the conversation as the server sees it. Each [turn](#turn) appends exactly one [interaction](#interaction). Used by the [projection](#projection) stage to build the next [prompt](#prompt).

### Interaction

A single user-and-assistant exchange within a [dialog](#dialog). Holds the user message, the assistant response, any retrieved [knowledge components](#knowledge-component), and (when diagnostics are on) per-node debug information.

______________________________________________________________________

## Graphs, nodes, and workflows

### Workflow

The overall per-turn behaviour of an [agent](#agent) — what happens between receiving the user message and emitting `TurnComplete`. A workflow is defined by a [graph](#graph) of [nodes](#node) and is compiled from a `GraphDescription` when the agent is created.

### Graph

A declarative description of a [workflow](#workflow): a list of [nodes](#node), where each node's typed params carry both its configuration and its [exit](#exit-route) wiring, plus a start node name. Built client-side with the graph builder APIs, validated server-side at agent creation. Compilation failures surface as error `3003` (see [error codes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html)).

### Node

A single unit of computation within a [graph](#graph). Each node has a typed parameter struct containing both its configuration and one or more named [exit](#exit-route) fields, and well-defined side effects on the [dialog](#dialog). See [Workflow Nodes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/index.html) for the full, current catalog of built-in node types.

### Exit route

A named output of a [node](#node). Each exit is encoded as a typed string field on the node's params object using the naming convention `<exit_name>_exit` (e.g. `triggered_exit`, `not_triggered_exit`). An empty string routes the turn to end-of-turn; any non-empty value names the next node to execute. For example, `RegexGuardrailNode` has `triggered` and `not_triggered` exits; `ToolCallNode` has `tool_called` and `no_tool_called`.

### Projection

The stage that turns the [dialog](#dialog) plus retained state into a [prompt](#prompt) for a [language model](#language-model). For `Generate` nodes, projection also renders the node's [Mustache template](#mustache-template) against the current turn's [instruction slots](#instruction-slot) and [knowledge components](#knowledge-component), then splices the result into the prompt at the configured placement. A token budget with hysteresis ensures the prompt fits inside the model's context window. When a [rolling summary](#rolling-summary) is present, history replay starts after the newest fold. See the [projection concept page](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/projection-and-token-budgets.html).

### Rolling summary

The compressed record of interactions a [Summarize node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/summarize.html) has [folded](#fold). Projection appends the newest summary to the system message and replays the [dialog](#dialog) only after `covered_through`. Older summaries stay in the dialog as history and are not rendered. The summary is part of an exported dialog snapshot.

### Fold

One summarizer pass. It rewrites the [rolling summary](#rolling-summary) from the previous summary plus the interactions that have aged out of the hot window (`keep_recent_turns`). A fold that does not fit the summarizer's own context covers the largest chronological prefix that does, and leaves the rest for a later fold.

### Mustache template

A [Mustache](https://mustache.github.io/) source string attached to a `Generate` node via the `template` param. Before each model call, [projection](#projection) renders it against a context that includes `{{user_message}}`, the `{{#instructions}}` list from [instruction slots](#instruction-slot), and the `{{#knowledge}}` list from [knowledge components](#knowledge-component). The rendered text is spliced into the [prompt](#prompt) at the position specified by the `placement` param. See the [Use Mustache Templates how-to](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-mustache-templates.html).

### Classify Intent node

A [node](#node) type that maps a user message to a discrete intent label by top-1 vector similarity search over a small, labelled [embedded string storage](#embedded-string-storage). On a match it attaches an intention component to the current [interaction](#interaction) for a downstream [Intent to Instruction node](#intent-to-instruction-node) to consume; it generates no text and renders nothing into the [prompt](#prompt). See the [Classify Intent reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent.html).

### Intent to Instruction node

A [node](#node) type that looks up the intent label written by a preceding [Classify Intent node](#classify-intent-node) in a `Map`-kind [string storage](#string-storage) and attaches the matching value as an [instruction slot](#instruction-slot) to the current [interaction](#interaction). The downstream [Generate node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html) then renders it via its [Mustache template](#mustache-template). It always takes the `default` exit. See the [Intent to Instruction reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/intent-to-instruction.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## Knowledge, retrieval, and storage

### RAG

Retrieval-Augmented Generation. An approach that injects topically relevant text snippets into the [prompt](#prompt) so the [language model](#language-model) can ground its answer on content the model itself does not "know". In Tryll, RAG is implemented by a [Retrieve node](#retrieve-node) in front of a [Generate node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html).

### Retrieval

The act of selecting the snippets from a knowledge source that best match the current query. Dense retrieval (the default) ranks by cosine distance to the query [embedding](#embedding); lexical retrieval ranks by BM25 keyword score; hybrid runs both and fuses the rankings with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Produces [knowledge components](#knowledge-component) that the workflow may or may not present to the model.

### Retrieve node

A [node](#node) type that searches an [embedded string storage](#embedded-string-storage) (dense, lexical, or hybrid [retrieval](#retrieval)) and attaches the top-`k` matches to the current [interaction](#interaction) as [knowledge components](#knowledge-component). See the [Retrieve reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve.html).

### Knowledge base

Synonym for "vector index used by a [Retrieve node](#retrieve-node)". In Tryll, a knowledge base is realised as an [embedded string storage](#embedded-string-storage).

### Instruction slot

A named instruction string attached to the current [interaction](#interaction) as a `kind=Instruction` [slot](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/slots-and-inter-node-value-passing.html) by an [Instruction node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/instruction.html) (or [Intent to Instruction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/intent-to-instruction.html)). [Projection](#projection) exposes instruction slots to the downstream `Generate` node's [Mustache template](#mustache-template) as: `{{slot.<name>}}` (direct lookup) and entries in the `{{#instructions}}` list (each with `{{name}}` and `{{text}}`).

### Knowledge component

A single piece of retrieved or attached text plus metadata (source, score, chunk id). Multiple components may attach to one [interaction](#interaction). [Projection](#projection) exposes them to the `Generate` node's [Mustache template](#mustache-template) as the `{{#knowledge}}` list and `{{#knowledge_<source>}}` direct-lookup sections.

### Chunk

A bounded slice of source text that has been offline-embedded and stored in an [embedded string storage](#embedded-string-storage). Chunking happens at index build time, not at query time; each [retrieval](#retrieval) result is one chunk.

### Embedding

A dense floating-point vector that represents the semantic content of a piece of text. Produced by an [embedding model](#embedding-model); compared via cosine distance inside an [HNSW](#hnsw) index.

### Embedding model

A [model](#language-model) whose output is an [embedding](#embedding) rather than generated text. Declared in the [model catalog](#model-catalog) with `"model_type": "embedding"`. Referenced by name from `RetrieveNode` parameters or from an [embedded string storage](#embedded-string-storage) config file.

### HNSW

Hierarchical Navigable Small World — the approximate-nearest-neighbour index structure used by Tryll's [embedded string storage](#embedded-string-storage). Optimised for fast cosine-distance search over large vector sets.

### String storage

A named, session-owned container of plain strings. Created via `CreateStringStorageRequest` (inline array or file path). Consumed by [canned-response](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/canned-response.html) and [regex-guardrail](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/regex-guardrail.html) nodes, which pick or match one string per invocation. Not embedded, not indexed. See the [string storage reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/string-storage.html).

### Embedded string storage

A session-owned vector index built from strings plus a precomputed [HNSW](#hnsw) file. Two construction paths: a directory containing a `*.kb.json` config plus a `*.usearch` file (Path A), or an inline array of strings that the server embeds on demand (Path B). Consumed by [Retrieve nodes](#retrieve-node). See the [embedded string storage reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/embedded-string-storage.html).

### Canned response

A fixed reply selected from a [string storage](#string-storage). The [canned-response node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/canned-response.html) emits one string from its backing storage (`RoundRobin` by default, or `Random` or `First`) and terminates the turn without invoking a [language model](#language-model). Useful for scripted answers and fallback paths.

### Guardrail

A pattern-matching check that gates workflow flow. The [regex-guardrail node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/regex-guardrail.html) runs an input slot (default `user_message`) against a [string storage](#string-storage) of patterns and routes the turn to `triggered` or `not_triggered` accordingly. Common use: short-circuit unsafe or off-topic inputs to a [canned response](#canned-response).

______________________________________________________________________

## Models and inference

### Language model

A model that takes a text [prompt](#prompt) and emits generated text token-by-token. In the Tryll catalog, language models omit the `model_type` field entirely — language is the implicit default. See the [models concept page](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/models-and-inference-engines.html).

### SLM

Small Language Model — a [language model](#language-model) small enough to run on consumer hardware (CPU, integrated GPU, or a single consumer GPU). Tryll is designed around SLMs: on-device inference, no cloud round-trip, and aggressive KV-cache management.

### Inference engine

The backend runtime that executes a [model](#language-model). Each [model catalog](#model-catalog) entry names its engine, and every [variant](#model-variant) of that entry shares it. The session does not choose an engine: `CreateSessionRequest.model_config` may carry optional `(role, engine)` hints, which only let the server initialise those engines early. The default build runs llama.cpp (`LlamaCpp`), Sherpa-ONNX (`SherpaOnnx`, for STT and TTS), and ONNX Runtime (`OnnxRuntime`). `OnnxGenAI`, `WindowsML`, `OpenVino`, and `TensorRtLlm` are `InferenceEngine` enum slots reserved for future engines.

### GGUF

The binary file format used by `llama.cpp` for quantised [language models](#language-model). Tryll downloads GGUF files from HuggingFace for catalog entries whose [inference engine](#inference-engine) is `llama.cpp`.

### LoRA adapter

A small [GGUF](#gguf) file, fine-tuned for one base [language model](#language-model), that changes how that model behaves for a narrow job. An LLM node runs its model with up to 8 adapters, each with a scale (`1` = as trained, `0` = off), listed in the node's `adaptation` table. Fixed when the agent is created. See [Use a LoRA Adapter](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-a-lora-adapter.html).

### Model catalog

The server's `models.json` file — the authoritative list of models Tryll can download, load, and run. Each catalog entry declares a name, a purpose (`model_type`: `language` — the default when the field is omitted — `embedding`, `stt`, `tts`, or `vad`), default sampling parameters, and one or more [variants](#model-variant). See the [model management reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/model-management.html).

### Model variant

One concrete packaging of a catalogued model, such as one GGUF quantisation. All variants of one catalog entry share a single [inference engine](#inference-engine), and loading the model uses that engine. `LoadModelRequest` takes a model name and an optional memory placement hint; it does not select an engine or a variant.

### Variant

Short form of [model variant](#model-variant).

### Pinned retention

A model-loading policy that keeps a language / embedding / STT / TTS model resident in memory until an explicit `UnloadModelRequest` (and no live users remain). Suitable for the hot model(s) on a given machine. Opposite of [OnDemand retention](#ondemand-retention). VAD catalog entries are not pin/unloadable.

### OnDemand retention

A model-loading policy that loads a language / embedding / STT / TTS model when an [agent](#agent) (or voice input / TTS / embedding use) needs it and unloads it when unused — after `DestroyAgent`, or when the next validated model load sweeps idle OnDemand entries across all four caches. Trades memory for latency. Opposite of [Pinned retention](#pinned-retention).

### Context (KV)

The KV cache — the per-model tensor of cached attention keys and values for every [token](#token) the model has processed this turn. Tryll reuses as much KV state as possible across [turns](#turn) when the [prompt](#prompt) prefix is stable; this is what makes conversational inference fast.

### TTS

Text-to-speech — turning text into spoken audio. The [Generate and Speak node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate-and-speak.html) voices generated tokens sentence by sentence as they stream; the [Speak node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/speak.html) voices a slot's text. Both speak with the agent's [voice profile](#voice-profile); neither node has voice settings of its own.

### Voice profile

An [agent](#agent)'s one voice (`VoiceProfile`): the TTS model from the [model catalog](#model-catalog) (`tts_model_name`, required), the base identity (`speaker_id`, a reference clip, or a voice description), speed, language, `emit_visemes`, and named [delivery modes](#delivery-mode). Passed at `CreateAgent` and replaced with `SetAgentVoice`. Every speaking node of the agent uses it, so one workflow can serve many characters. See [Voice Profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html).

### Delivery mode

A named way of speaking that a [voice profile](#voice-profile) defines, such as `angry` or `whisper`. Game code switches it with `SetAgentDeliveryMode`, which applies from the next sentence. `neutral` is built in and means the plain voice. What a mode can change depends on the TTS model: a different reference clip, a Maya1 delivery clause, the Chatterbox exaggeration, or only speed. See [Voice Profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html#delivery-modes) and [Add Emotions to a Voice](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/add-emotions-to-a-voice.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## Prompts, tokens, and streaming

### Prompt

The concatenated input passed to the [language model](#language-model) at [generation](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html) time: system preamble, projected [dialog](#dialog), attached [knowledge](#knowledge-component), tool descriptions, and the current user message. Produced by [projection](#projection).

### Token

The atomic unit the [language model](#language-model) reads and emits. Each model has its own tokenizer; token counts for the same text differ between models. Token budgets in [projection](#projection) are measured in tokens of the active model.

### Token budget

The number of [tokens](#token) a language-model node's [projected](#projection) [prompt](#prompt) may use: that node's context size minus the headroom reserved for the generated response. Each node trims its own prompt; there is no per-agent setting. Exceeding the budget triggers dialog truncation with hysteresis.

### Streaming

The mode in which the server emits generated text in chunks rather than waiting for the full response. Each chunk arrives as an `AnswerText` frame carrying only the new text (`is_delta = true`). The last chunk from each node carries `is_final = true`; for streamed output it is an empty terminator. `TurnComplete` follows once the turn ends. See [how to stream answers to a UI](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/stream-answers-to-ui.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## Tool calling

### Tool call

A structured instruction emitted by a [language model](#language-model) indicating it wants to invoke a named external function. In Tryll, tool calls are **detected only** — the server parses them from model output and returns them to the client, which is responsible for execution. See the [tool calling concept page](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/tool-calling.html).

### Tool-call format

The specific textual convention the [language model](#language-model) uses to express a [tool call](#tool-call). Tryll follows the model's own chat template for both prompting and parsing, so there is nothing to choose. The `tool_call_format` field on the [tool-call node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/tool-call.html) is deprecated and ignored by the server.

______________________________________________________________________

## Constrained decoding

### Constrained decoding

Forcing a [language model](#language-model)'s output to match a formal [grammar](#gbnf) at every decode step: tokens that could not legally continue the output are masked out before sampling, so malformed output is impossible (not merely discouraged). Also called grammar-constrained generation. In Tryll it is exposed via the `grammar` param on [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html) and [Generate and Speak](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate-and-speak.html) nodes. It guarantees the output's *shape*, never its *meaning* — a constrained model can still emit a valid-but-wrong answer. See the [constrained output concept page](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/constrained-output.html).

### GBNF

GGML BNF — the grammar notation used by `llama.cpp` (and therefore by Tryll's `grammar` param) to describe [constrained](#constrained-decoding) output. A grammar is a set of `name ::= …` rules over string literals, alternation (`|`), and sequences; it must define a rule named `root` and must not be left-recursive. See the [upstream GBNF guide](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/grammars/README.md) for the full syntax.

______________________________________________________________________

## Transport

### Wire protocol

The byte-level contract between the Tryll client and server: TCP transport, 4-byte little-endian length prefix, FlatBuffers payload, 1 MiB max frame. See the [wire protocol reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## Editor tools

### Chat Window

An editor-only window (`Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Chat` in Unity, `Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Tryll Chat` in Unreal) that creates its own agent from a scene component and lets you converse with it without entering Play mode. Hosts the [turn inspector](#turn-inspector) in a side pane. See [Test an agent in the editor](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/test-agent-in-editor.html).

### Dialog Lab

An editor-only window that runs one scripted [dialog](#dialog) across parameter variants and seeds, then shows every result side by side so the spread is visible. Makes no quality claim — it shows raw output, deterministic checks, and timings. Ships in both editors. See [Compare dialog variants](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/compare-dialog-variants.html).

### Agent Log

An editor-only window that records what this editor process sent to and received from each [agent](#agent) — turns, voice transcripts the client sent, deferred variable flushes, and lifecycle events — as a per-agent narrative rather than an event dump. Scoped to **one client connection**, not the whole server. See [Use the Agent Log](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-agent-log.html).

### Turn inspector

The shared panel that explains a single [turn](#turn): which [nodes](#node) ran and via which [exit routes](#exit-route), per-node timing, the node parameters used, the rendered [prompt](#prompt) and output, [retrieval](#retrieval) hits, and [tool calls](#tool-call). One implementation, hosted by the [Chat Window](#chat-window), [Agent Log](#agent-log), and [Dialog Lab](#dialog-lab). See the [turn inspector reference](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-inspector.html).

### Turn diagnostics

The per-turn `debug_info` payload the server attaches when an [agent](#agent) was created with `enable_diagnostics`. It is the data the [turn inspector](#turn-inspector) renders. The flag is **structural** — it cannot be enabled on an agent that already exists.

### Server monitor

A contributor-facing browser UI served by a dev-time HTTP/SSE sidecar in the server process. Sees every [session](#session) on the server, which is its advantage over the [Agent Log](#agent-log); it cannot see what a client sent, which is the Agent Log's. Compiled out of Production builds.

# Agent Parameters

Every [agent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#agent) in Tryll is created by a single wire frame: `CreateAgentRequest`. This page documents every field on that request, grouped by what it controls:

1. The [graph](#graph) the agent will run.
1. The [fallback model](#default-model) every language-model node uses by default.
1. [Diagnostics](#diagnostics).
1. The agent's [variables](#variables) declaration.
1. [KV-cache initialization](#kv-cache-initialization).
1. The agent's [workload](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html#inference-throttle-and-agent-workload) class.
1. The agent's [voice](#voice).

The authoritative source for every shape below is the [wire protocol](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html).

Changing parameters after creation

Many node parameters can be updated after the agent is created and while it is idle. See [Change Agent Parameters at Runtime](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/change-agent-parameters.html) for the full list and API examples.

## Overview

| Field                       | Type                         | Required           | Default        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `request_id`                | uint64                       | Yes                | —              | Client-assigned correlation id. Echoed on `CreateAgentResponse` and on any `ErrorResponse` replacing it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `graph`                     | `GraphDescription`           | Yes                | —              | The workflow graph. See [Graph](#graph).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `default_model_name`        | string                       | No                 | `""`           | Fallback model name for language-model nodes (Generate, GenerateAndSpeak, ToolCall, ClassifyIntentLLM, Summarize) that do not set their own `model_name` param. Empty = no default; every such node must supply its own. See [Default model](#default-model).                                                                                                                              |
| `enable_diagnostics`        | bool                         | No                 | `false`        | When `true`, the server serialises per-node execution data into `TurnComplete.debug_info`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `maintain_dialogue_history` | bool                         | No                 | `true`         | When `true` (default) the agent keeps its full dialogue history across turns. When `false` the history is cleared after each turn completes — a **stateless agent** whose turns start with only the system prompt and the new message. Useful for technical agents (classification, routing, tool-picking) that gain nothing from prior turns and should not pay to store or project them. |
| `variables`                 | `[AgentVariable]`            | No                 | `[]`           | The agent's **complete** variable declaration — every variable it will ever have, with its initial value. The value's type fixes that variable's type for the agent's lifetime; post-create writes to an undeclared name are rejected. See [Variables](#variables).                                                                                                                        |
| `kv_cache_initialization`   | `AgentKvCacheInitialization` | No                 | `AllocateOnly` | How the agent's language-model KV caches are prepared at creation: `AllocateOnly` (default), `Prefill`, or `DeferAllocation`. See [KV-cache initialization](#kv-cache-initialization).                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `workload`                  | `AgentWorkload`              | No                 | `Interactive`  | Scheduling hint, fixed for the agent's lifetime: `Interactive` (default) or `Background` for agents nobody waits on, which the inference scheduler paces or defers first under load. See [Inference throttle and agent workload](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html#inference-throttle-and-agent-workload).                                                    |
| `voice`                     | `VoiceProfile`               | When a node speaks | absent         | The agent's one voice: TTS model, identity, `emit_visemes` and delivery modes. Required when the graph has a `Speak` or `GenerateAndSpeak` node. See [Voice](#voice).                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

A `CreateAgentRequest` is rejected with error [`3003`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent) `GraphCompilationFailed` if any graph validation rule below fails. Voice errors have their own codes; see [Voice](#voice).

______________________________________________________________________

## Graph

`GraphDescription` carries the full topology of the agent's workflow.

| Field        | Type                | Description                                                            |
| ------------ | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `nodes`      | `[NodeDescription]` | List of every [node](#nodedescription) in the graph. At least one.     |
| `start_node` | string              | Name of the node where execution begins. Must match a node in `nodes`. |

Wiring between nodes is encoded in each node's typed **params** object, not in a separate list. Each declared exit has a corresponding `<exit_name>_exit` field (e.g. `default_exit`, `triggered_exit`). An **empty string** routes the turn to END. A **non-empty string** must name another node in `nodes` — the server rejects graphs where an exit field names a missing node with error [`3003 GraphCompilationFailed`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent).

### `NodeDescription`

| Field         | Type        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | string      | Node instance name. Unique within the graph. Also the default `source` label on Retrieve.                                                                                                                                           |
| `params_type` | union tag   | Selects the typed params table variant (`GenerateParams`, `RegexGuardrailParams`, etc.).                                                                                                                                            |
| `params`      | typed table | The typed params table for this node type. Contains configuration fields (model name, prompts, …) **and** exit fields (`default_exit`, `triggered_exit`, …). Each node's reference page lists all available params and exit fields. |

### `ToolDefinition`

Tool schemas are not a `NodeDescription` field. They live on the Tool Call node's own params, in `ToolCallParams.tools: [ToolDefinition]`.

| Field         | Type                    | Description                                                      |
| ------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | string                  | Tool name exposed to the model.                                  |
| `description` | string                  | Short description shown to the model as part of the tool prompt. |
| `parameters`  | `[ToolParamDefinition]` | Parameter schema for the tool.                                   |

#### `ToolParamDefinition`

| Field         | Type   | Description                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`        | string | Parameter name.                                                                                                  |
| `type`        | string | Type hint as a string (e.g. `"string"`, `"integer"`). Model-facing only; the server does not validate arguments. |
| `description` | string | Short description of the parameter.                                                                              |

See [Tool Call node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/tool-call.html) and the [tool-calling concept page](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/tool-calling.html) for how the server uses these definitions.

______________________________________________________________________

## Default model

`default_model_name` is a fallback used by language-model nodes that omit their own `model_name` param: Generate, GenerateAndSpeak, ToolCall, ClassifyIntentLLM, and Summarize. Speak, and the speech half of GenerateAndSpeak, take their TTS model from the agent's [voice](#voice) (`voice.tts_model_name`) and never use this field. Leaving it empty is legal — every such node must then supply `model_name` itself; any node missing both results in a compilation failure.

Naming resolves against the [model catalog](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#model-catalog) (`models.json`). The server loads the model on demand if it is not already resident; see [model management](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/model-management.html#lifecycle).

______________________________________________________________________

## Diagnostics

When `enable_diagnostics = true`, every `TurnComplete` carries a JSON string in `debug_info` describing what the turn did: the nodes it ran and the [exit route](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#exit-route) each took, the prompt every model received, what each node produced, and engine counters. **[Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html) documents every field**, including why a given key may be absent.

`enable_diagnostics` is **structural**: it is fixed for the agent's lifetime and cannot be turned on for an agent that already exists. Two server-side flags in [`server-config.json`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/server-configuration.html) trim the payload further — `include_engine_diagnostics` removes the `engine` sections, and `include_interaction_in_diagnostics` removes the end-of-turn [interaction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#interaction) snapshot.

The default is `false` — no diagnostics, zero overhead. Flip it on for debug sessions only; payloads grow linearly with graph size and knowledge component count.

The editor tooling manages this for you: the Chat Window enables it on the agent it creates, and the [Agent Log](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-agent-log.html) holds a lease so agents created while it is open request diagnostics too. See [How to define and handle tool calls](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/define-and-handle-tool-calls.html) for a worked example that turns diagnostics on to inspect the tool-call detection path.

______________________________________________________________________

## Variables

`variables` declares the agent's typed per-agent key→value store, **complete** at creation. Each `AgentVariable` carries a name and an initial value whose active type (`int64` / `double` / `string` / `bool` / `set<string>`) fixes that variable's type for the agent's lifetime.

- Consumed by Mustache templates as `{{var.<name>}}`, by the Retrieve / ClassifyIntent filter grammar as a `{"var": "<name>"}` operand, and — when a `Generate` / `GenerateAndSpeak` node sets `substitute_agent_variables` — by `__NAME__` marker substitution in streamed output.
- Mutated over the wire with `UpdateAgentVariablesRequest`; writes to an undeclared name are rejected locally without a round-trip. An invalid declaration fails creation with [`3015 InvalidVariableValue`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent); runtime write errors are [`3013 UnknownVariable`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent) and [`3014 VariableTypeMismatch`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent).

See [Concept: Agent Variables](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/agent-variables.html) and the how-tos [Drive prompts and retrieval from game state](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/drive-prompts-and-retrieval-from-game-state.html) and [Substitute agent variables in LLM output](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/substitute-agent-variables-in-output.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## Voice

`voice` is the agent's [voice profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html): the TTS model (`tts_model_name`, required), the base identity (`speaker_id`, `reference_voice` or `voice_description`), `speed`, `lang`, `emit_visemes`, and named delivery modes. Every speaking node of the agent uses it; the nodes hold no voice settings.

- **Required when the graph speaks.** If any node is a `Speak` or `GenerateAndSpeak` and `voice` is absent, creation fails with [`3025 AgentVoiceRequired`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent). There is no default voice.
- **Optional otherwise.** An agent whose graph never speaks loads no TTS model, even with a voice. It cannot be given a voice later, so pass one at creation if you will need `SetAgentVoice` or `SetAgentDeliveryMode`.
- **Validated when set.** A field the model cannot use, a missing clip, or an unknown model fails creation with [`3023 InvalidVoiceProfile`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent); a session language the model does not declare fails with [`3017 ModelLanguageUnsupported`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent).
- **Not a node parameter.** `ChangeAgentParam` cannot change it. Replace it with `SetAgentVoiceRequest` (idle only) and switch its delivery mode with `SetAgentDeliveryModeRequest` (any time).

See [Voice Profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html) for every field and rule.

______________________________________________________________________

## KV-cache initialization

`kv_cache_initialization` chooses how the agent's eligible language-model contexts (LLM nodes only — embeddings and all STT/TTS models, including the llama.cpp voices Orpheus and Maya1, are unaffected) are prepared when the agent is created:

| Value                    | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `AllocateOnly` (default) | Allocate each context's KV cache but do not decode anything yet.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `Prefill`                | Allocate **and** decode each context's reusable prefix up front, so the first turn skips that cost. Prefill failure surfaces as [`4004 KvCacheOperationFailed`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#4xxx-inference-workflow). |
| `DeferAllocation`        | Defer even allocation until the first send.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Idle agents also support the aggregate `PrefillAgentKvCache`, `EvictAgentKvCache`, and `GetAgentKvCacheStatus` operations; eligible contexts are restored automatically before every send. See [Manage an agent's KV cache](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/manage-agent-kv-cache.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## Minimum working example

```
# Minimal agent with no Retrieve nodes
from tryll_client.graph import GraphDescription, GenerateParams

graph = (
    GraphDescription()
    .add_node("answer", GenerateParams())
    .set_start_node("answer")
    .set_default_model_name("My Local Model")
)

agent = client.create_agent(graph)
```

```
using namespace Tryll::Client;
using namespace Tryll::NodeParams;

GenerateParamsT gp;
// default_exit defaults to "" (END)

GraphDescription graph;
graph.AddGenerate("answer", std::move(gp))
     .SetStartNode("answer")
     .SetDefaultModelName("My Local Model");

auto agent = client.CreateAgent(graph);
```

```
UTryllGenerateParams* P = UTryllNodeParamsFactory::MakeGenerateParams(this);
// DefaultExit defaults to TEXT("") (END)

FTryllGraphDescription Graph = FTryllGraphBuilder()
    .AddNode(TEXT("answer"), P)
    .SetStartNode(TEXT("answer"))
    .SetDefaultModelName(TEXT("My Local Model"))
    .Build();
```

Or author the equivalent inside a `UTryllWorkflowAsset` and assign it to the `UTryllAgentComponent`.

For an agent with Retrieve + Mustache template, see [How to create a simple RAG assistant](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/create-simple-rag-assistant.html) and [How to use Mustache templates](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-mustache-templates.html).

## Client bindings

- **C++:** `Tryll::Client::TryllClient::CreateAgent` + `Tryll::Client::GraphDescription` — `TryllClient.h`, `GraphDescription.h`
- **Python:** `tryll_client.TryllClient.create_agent` + `tryll_client.GraphDescription` — `client.py`, `graph.py`
- **Unreal:** `UTryllAgentComponent::CreateAgent` / `FTryllGraphDescription` / `UTryllWorkflowAsset` — `TryllGraphDescription.h`

# Turn Inspector

The **turn inspector** is the panel that explains a single turn: which nodes ran, how long each took, what prompt the model actually received, what it produced, and what the turn retrieved or called along the way.

It is **one component with three hosts**. The same blocks, in the same order, with the same behaviour, appear in:

| Host                                                                                | Where (Unity / Unreal)                                              | How you select a turn     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| [Chat Window](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/test-agent-in-editor.html)   | `Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Chat` / `Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Tryll Chat`             | Click an assistant bubble |
| [Agent Log](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-agent-log.html)            | `Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Agent Log` / `Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Tryll Agent Log`   | Click a received turn row |
| [Dialog Lab](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/compare-dialog-variants.html) | `Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Dialog Lab` / `Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Tryll Dialog Lab` | Click a grid cell         |

This page is the reference for the panel itself. Each host page covers only what is specific to that host — how turns get selected there, and what else that window does.

Prerequisite: diagnostics must be on

The inspector renders the `debug_info` payload a turn carries, which requires `enable_diagnostics` at `CreateAgent`. That flag is **structural** — it cannot be turned on for an agent that already exists.

You do not normally set it yourself. Chat enables it for the agent it creates, and the Agent Log holds a diagnostics-demand lease so agents created while it is open request diagnostics too. Neither writes to your scene or assets. The consequence is that the Agent Log must be **open before an agent is created** to get depth on that agent's turns — see [Use the Agent Log](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-agent-log.html#open-before-you-create-agents).

______________________________________________________________________

## The one thing to understand first: everything is node-attributed

A Tryll turn is a graph run, not a single model call. A turn can run a classifier, then a retriever, then a generator — each with its own parameters, its own prompt, and its own output.

So every block below the Route breadcrumb reads **per node execution**, not per turn. A graph with two `Retrieve` nodes shows two hit tables. A graph with a classifier and a generator shows two prompt subsections, each with its own heading (`#2 answer (GenerateNode) [default]`).

**Click a node chip in the Route breadcrumb to narrow the entire panel to that one node** — its parameters, its prompt, its retrieval hits. Click the same chip again to go back to the whole turn. This is the fastest way to answer "what exactly did the classifier see?" in a multi-node graph, and it is the primary navigation control of the panel.

The one block node scope does **not** narrow is Raw JSON, which always shows the whole turn.

______________________________________________________________________

## Block reference

| Block               | Shown when                                                  | Starts    | Copy |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------- | ---- |
| **Route**           | Always                                                      | Expanded  | —    |
| **Timing**          | Always                                                      | Expanded  | —    |
| **Parameters**      | Diagnostics present                                         | Collapsed | —    |
| **Checks**          | Dialog Lab only, with authored checks                       | Expanded  | —    |
| **Prompt & output** | A node produced a prompt or output                          | Expanded  | ✅   |
| **Retrieval**       | The turn ran a `Retrieve` node                              | Expanded  | —    |
| **Intent**          | The turn ran a `ClassifyIntent` or `ClassifyIntentLLM` node | Expanded  | —    |
| **Tool calls**      | The turn ran a `ToolCall` node                              | Expanded  | —    |
| **Errors**          | The turn ended in error or cancellation                     | Expanded  | —    |
| **Raw JSON**        | Always                                                      | Collapsed | ✅   |

A block with nothing to say is **hidden, not rendered empty**. If you do not see Retrieval, the turn did not retrieve.

### Route

The execution order, as a breadcrumb of `node name [exit taken]` chips — one chip per node *execution*, so a node entered twice appears twice.

Chips are **selectable**: click one to scope the whole panel to that node, click it again to clear the scope. The scoped chip is highlighted and the Route header's trailing text changes to `<node> only`.

"Other branch" exits (`not_found`, `triggered`, `no_tool_called`) are coloured distinctly from errors — they are usually correct behaviour, not failures.

If the turn never executed, the block says so rather than rendering an empty breadcrumb.

### Timing

A stacked bar of per-node duration, plus the turn total in the header.

- Each node gets a segment sized by its own `duration_s`. Nodes that took no measurable time render grey at zero width — a model-free node like `Branch` or `Transform` normally does.
- **Time to first token** is marked separately: the delay before the first token arrived, which is the number that governs perceived responsiveness.
- Pause-related figures (`paused_duration_s`, `pause_count`) appear for turns that paused.

### Parameters

The parameters each node actually ran with, dumped from the turn's `diagnostics.parameters` grouped under a heading per node.

This is **the parameters the server records into diagnostics, not every field on the node**. Some node fields are deliberately not recorded. When a value is an array — a `ToolCall` node's `tools` signatures, for instance — the elements stack down the value column rather than collapsing to a bare count.

Starts collapsed, because on most turns it restates configuration you already know.

### Checks

**Dialog Lab only.** The authored deterministic checks for that step — Must Contain, Must Not Contain, Regex Forbid, Max Words — with pass/fail per check. The header shows `N failed` or `all passed`.

The other two hosts have no authored checks, so the block is absent there rather than empty.

### Prompt & output

The block most often worth opening. For each node that prompted a model, it shows the **rendered prompt in the form actually sent** — system, user and assistant messages as the model received them — followed by what that node generated.

This is where projection becomes visible: history replay, `{{#instructions}}` blocks, knowledge components and Mustache slot substitution have all already happened in what you see here. If a prompt does not contain what you expected, this block is where that shows up.

**Copy** on the header lifts the transcript to the clipboard without expanding the section. When a node scope is active it copies the scoped node only, matching what is on screen.

Dialog Lab: two-sided prompt diff

Pinning two cells in the Lab (⇧-click, or the ⊙ in a column header) turns this block into a line diff — green `+` for lines only in the selected cell, red `−` for lines only in the other. The red side is usually the interesting one: it shows what a variant *dropped*. Each node is diffed against its own counterpart, and a node that ran on only one side is called out as such.

### Retrieval

One subsection per `Retrieve` node execution. The header is a funnel — `input.query` → `raw_result_count` → `filtered_count` → `result_count` — with `threshold`, `top_k` and the storage name.

The body is the hit table: each retrieved chunk with its distance, in server order (which for Hybrid retrieval is RRF rank). Rows beyond the threshold are dimmed rather than removed, so you can see the near-misses that did not make it in. A null distance renders as `—`.

See [Retrieve](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve.html) and [Embedded String Storage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/embedded-string-storage.html).

### Intent

One subsection per `ClassifyIntent` or `ClassifyIntentLLM` execution in scope. The header summarises the decision — `ask_wing · found`, or `not_found · below_threshold` — and a `found` exit is coloured as success, `not_found` as a warning. `not_found` is usually correct behaviour, not a failure.

The block is **hidden when the turn ran no classifier**, including Generate-only graphs. `IntentToInstruction` is not a classifier: it is a lookup, and its result stays in Parameters. Click a Route chip to narrow the block to that one execution.

**Embedding** (`ClassifyIntent`). A muted funnel line (`query → storage · metadata_field · threshold`), then either a winner card (intent, distance, id, index, record text) or a rejected pick (`rejected ask_wing @ 0.3120 (threshold 0.25)`). A top-k table lists ranked candidates; rows beyond the threshold are dimmed rather than removed. A null distance renders as `—`.

**LLM** (`ClassifyIntentLLM`). A muted line (`model · threshold · margin · history_turns`), a horizontal probability bar per candidate (sorted by probability, ties keep `intents_ids` order), and the `predicted_letter` / `top_prob` / `second_prob` / `margin_result` strip. The winning or rejected label is shown in words — you do not map the letter by hand. A `probs` / `intents_ids` length mismatch draws a warning and shows only the common prefix.

When the turn's interaction components are present, a footer lists the labels that were actually attached: `attached to dialog: ask_wing`. When `include_interaction_in_diagnostics` is off, that footer is omitted silently. Unlike [Tool calls](#tool-calls), this block does not depend on interaction diagnostics — the classification itself is always in `output.classification`.

`notify_client` does not gate this block. A classifier with `notify_client` left at `Disabled` still appears here; it simply produces no Agent Log event. See [Classify Intent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent.html) and [Classify Intent (LLM)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent-llm.html).

### Tool calls

For each `ToolCall` node execution: which function the model called, the arguments it passed, and the result that came back — as JSON. The header shows the call count and the exit taken.

A **parse fallback** chip appears when a node's `output.parse_fallback` is true: the output could not be parsed as a call, so no call was recorded. The line under it gives `output.parse_failure` and `output.parse_error` — whether the model attempted a call (`malformed_call`) or answered in prose (`no_call`), and where the parser stopped. See [Tool Call diagnostics](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/tool-call.html#diagnostics). If the player saw tool-call markup in the answer, see [Fix tool-call text in answers](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/fix-tool-call-text-in-answers.html).

Two things gate what appears here, and both are configuration rather than defects:

- **The node's `disposition`.** Whether a result is returned to the model at all, and whether the client is notified, is decided by `ToolCallParams.disposition`. A disposition that does not return results leaves the result side empty. See [Tool Call](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/tool-call.html).
- **Server config `include_interaction_in_diagnostics`.** Tool-call results are joined through the turn's interaction components. With this off, the panel explains that rather than silently rendering a short list.

### Errors

Present only for turns that ended in error or cancellation, carrying the terminal status and the error detail. The header shows the status.

### Raw JSON

The escape hatch: the complete `debug_info` payload the turn carried, pretty-printed. Everything above is a purpose-built view over this — so anything the panel has no dedicated block for is still reachable here.

The payload is shown **verbatim**: the editors add no keys, rename none, and drop none. Every field in it is documented in [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html), which is also the reference for the same payload as it arrives on the wire in `TurnComplete.debug_info`.

Unlike every other block, Raw JSON ignores the Route breadcrumb's node scope — it always shows the whole turn. **Copy** on the header puts the formatted JSON on the clipboard.

Two things currently live here and nowhere else:

- **Variable replacements and engine/scheduler counters**, including the KV-reuse figures that often explain why one sample was slower than another.

______________________________________________________________________

## When a block is missing or the panel is thin

The panel distinguishes these cases rather than rendering an empty section. If you see less than you expected, it is one of:

| What you see                         | Why                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Created before diagnostics capture" | The agent existed before the Agent Log opened. Recreate it, or create new agents while the window is open.    |
| "Unsupported schema"                 | The turn's `debug_info` is not `schema_version` 2. Raw JSON may still be offered.                             |
| "Turn was not executed"              | Dialog Lab: a seeded turn (injected without running the graph), or a turn after an error in the same column.  |
| A block simply absent                | The turn did not do that thing — no `Retrieve` node ran, no tool was called, no error occurred.               |
| Tool-call results empty              | The node's `disposition` does not return results, or `include_interaction_in_diagnostics` is off server-side. |

______________________________________________________________________

## Host differences

The panel is the same in all three windows and in both engines. What differs is its framing:

|                       | Chat                                         | Agent Log                                                 | Dialog Lab |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| Default visibility    | Visible                                      | Collapsed                                                 | Visible    |
| Width persisted       | Per window, independently of the other hosts | Per window                                                | Per window |
| Checks block          | —                                            | —                                                         | ✅         |
| Prompt diff (pinning) | —                                            | —                                                         | ✅         |
| Non-turn rows         | —                                            | Sent / system rows use a **different**, simpler inspector | —          |

In the Agent Log, only *received turn* rows open this panel. Sent rows and system rows are selectable too, but they open simpler panels showing the wire payload, deferred variable batches, and the server's `Ack` or error — see [Use the Agent Log](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-agent-log.html#the-inspector-changes-with-the-row).

Unity and Unreal parity

Both engines implement the same ten blocks in the same order. Chrome — fonts, splitter behaviour, scrollbar feel — differs, and that is expected.
