# TTS Models

Tryll synthesizes speech through two engines:

- [`SherpaOnnx`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/models-and-inference-engines.html) hosts **Supertonic 3** and **Pocket TTS**.
- [`LlamaCpp`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/models-and-inference-engines.html) hosts **Orpheus** and **Maya1**. Their audio codes are decoded by a shared SNAC 24 kHz decoder that runs on ONNX Runtime on the CPU.

A third engine, `onnx-runtime`, runs the Chatterbox family. Its catalog entries are internal and are not shipped.

llama.cpp also runs **Qwen3-TTS** (`Qwen3-TTS 12Hz 1.7B Base (Q4_K_M)`, family `qwen3tts`). It is a public catalog entry. It clones its voice from a reference clip, so the voice profile's `reference_voice` is required, and it speaks 10 languages through `lang`: zh, en, de, it, pt, es, ja, ko, fr, ru.

This page is the authoritative list of **which voices the Tryll server ships, which families it can load, and why the rest are out of reach**.

Short version: Tryll ships an **eSpeak-free** Sherpa-ONNX build so the server can be redistributed inside a proprietary game. That choice makes two Sherpa families available — **Supertonic 3** and **Pocket TTS** — and puts the rest of the Sherpa zoo out of reach. Separately, two llama.cpp SNAC voices — `Orpheus 3B FT (Q4_K_M)` and `Maya1 3B (i1-Q4_K_M)` — are public catalog entries. On Maya1, identity is the voice profile's `voice_description` and delivery is a delivery mode's `instruction`; `[emotion]` is not supported syntax.

Heavier SNAC quants (`Orpheus 3B FT (Q8)`, `Maya1 3B (Q8)`, `Maya1 3B (Q4_K_M)`) stay `audience: "internal"`. Release builds keep only `public` entries, so they are not in the shipped catalog at all.

For the catalog file format these models are declared in, see [Model Management](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/model-management.html). For the agent's voice settings, see [Voice Profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## Shipped voices

The four entries below are in the default `models.json`, are downloaded on demand, and are selected with `tts_model_name` on the agent's [voice profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html). Every speaking node of the agent ([`GenerateAndSpeak`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate-and-speak.html), [`Speak`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/speak.html)) uses that model. The engine is taken from the catalog — you do not pick Sherpa vs. llama.cpp in Project Settings. See [Choose where models run](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/choose-where-models-run.html).

| Catalog name             | Engine        | Family       | Voices                                                                            | Languages      | Voice cloning                                                | Weights license                             |
| ------------------------ | ------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `Supertonic 3 (int8)`    | `sherpa-onnx` | `supertonic` | 10 built-in styles (`speaker_id` `0`–`9`)                                         | 31, via `lang` | No                                                           | OpenRAIL-M (attribution + use restrictions) |
| `Pocket TTS (int8)`      | `sherpa-onnx` | `pocket`     | Single-speaker (`speaker_id` must stay `0`)                                       | English        | **Yes** — zero-shot from a reference WAV (`reference_voice`) | CC-BY-4.0 (attribution)                     |
| `Orpheus 3B FT (Q4_K_M)` | `llama-cpp`   | `orpheus`    | 8 named presets (`speaker_id` `0`–`7`: Tara, Leah, Jess, Leo, Dan, Mia, Zac, Zoe) | English        | No                                                           | Llama 3 Community License                   |
| `Maya1 3B (i1-Q4_K_M)`   | `llama-cpp`   | `maya1`      | 2 catalog presets (`speaker_id` `0`–`1`) or a natural-language description        | English        | No — describe the voice instead                              | Apache-2.0                                  |

Both SNAC voices pull a shared **SNAC 24 kHz decoder** (~50 MB) the first time either parent is downloaded. Deleting one parent does not delete the decoder.

Pick **Supertonic 3** when you want multiple distinct voices, non-English speech, or the lowest latency. Pick **Pocket TTS** when a character needs a specific voice you can supply as an audio sample — see [Clone a Voice](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/clone-a-voice.html). Pick **Orpheus** for named English speakers plus inline tags such as `<laugh>`. Pick **Maya1** when you want to brief a voice in natural language (`voice_description`) and steer delivery in words (a delivery mode's `instruction`).

Attribution is required

None of these weights are public domain.

- Supertonic 3 is OpenRAIL-M (attribution plus use-based restrictions — no impersonation or harmful use).
- Pocket TTS is CC-BY-4.0 (attribution).
- Orpheus weights are a Llama 3 derivative and inherit the [Llama 3 Community License](https://huggingface.co/canopylabs/orpheus-3b-0.1-ft); the Orpheus inference code is Apache-2.0.
- Maya1 weights are Apache-2.0.
- The shared SNAC decoder is MIT (`hubertsiuzdak/snac`).

If you ship a voice in a game, include the model attribution in your credits or third-party notices. The engine code itself (Sherpa-ONNX, ONNX Runtime, llama.cpp) is permissively licensed and imposes no such obligation.

______________________________________________________________________

## Voice controls by family

These are the [voice profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html) fields, by family. Do not encode identity or delivery as a spoken `[emotion]` prefix — that syntax is not supported. Model-native `<tag>` tokens that a catalog lists may reach the synthesizer; unknown tags are stripped from the audio copy only and do not rewrite history.

| Profile field               | Supertonic 3                                        | Pocket TTS                                                | Orpheus                                                                                 | Maya1                                                                                  | Qwen3-TTS Base                                                                                 |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `speaker_id`                | `0`–`9` (style index)                               | Must stay `0`                                             | `0`–`7` (named preset)                                                                  | `0`–`1` (catalog preset)                                                               | Must stay `0`                                                                                  |
| `reference_voice`           | Rejected                                            | Reference WAV (optional; falls back to the bundled voice) | Rejected                                                                                | Rejected                                                                               | Reference WAV (**required**; no default voice)                                                 |
| `voice_description`         | Rejected                                            | Rejected                                                  | Rejected                                                                                | Stable identity (overrides `speaker_id` when set)                                      | Rejected                                                                                       |
| Mode `instruction`          | Rejected                                            | Rejected                                                  | Rejected                                                                                | Sustained delivery while the mode is active                                            | Rejected                                                                                       |
| `lang`                      | 31 languages                                        | Rejected (English only)                                   | Rejected (English only)                                                                 | Rejected (English only)                                                                | 10 languages: zh, en, de, it, pt, es, ja, ko, fr, ru (only English is verified by listen-back) |
| `speed`, mode `speed_scale` | `0.1`–`3.0`                                         | `0.1`–`3.0`                                               | `1.0` only                                                                              | `1.0` only                                                                             | `1.0` only                                                                                     |
| Inline `<tag>` tokens       | None (every `<…>` span is stripped, with a warning) | None (every `<…>` span is stripped, with a warning)       | `<laugh>`, `<chuckle>`, `<sigh>`, `<cough>`, `<sniffle>`, `<groan>`, `<yawn>`, `<gasp>` | `<laugh>`, `<giggle>`, `<sigh>`, `<gasp>`, `<angry>`, `<whisper>`, `<cry>`, `<scream>` | None (every `<…>` span is stripped, with a warning)                                            |

"Rejected" means the voice fails with `3023 InvalidVoiceProfile` when it is set (at agent creation or `SetAgentVoice`), rather than being silently ignored. This includes a non-empty `lang` on an English-only voice. When `lang` is empty and the session locale is a language the voice does not declare (Pocket, Orpheus and Maya1 declare only `en`), the voice fails with `3017 ModelLanguageUnsupported`.

`voice_description` and `instruction` may be at most 1024 bytes and must not contain `"`, `<`, `>` or control characters (tab, CR and LF are allowed).

Orpheus, Maya1 and Qwen3-TTS synthesize **one call at a time per loaded model**: several NPCs sharing one of them wait for each other. The Sherpa voices have no such limit.

Maya1 catalog presets are starting points, not the only voices:

- `0` — *Male, 30s, American*
- `1` — *Female, 30s, American*

Set `voice_description` to something like *"Realistic female voice in the 30s with an American accent. Normal pitch, warm timbre, conversational pacing."* and the description replaces the preset. Add delivery modes with an `instruction` for delivery; `neutral` (no instruction) is the plain voice. These words map to trained delivery styles, matched as whole words: `whisper`, `angry` / `anger`, `happy` / `happily`, `sad` / `sadly`, `calm`, `excited`, `serious`, `sarcastic`, `disappointed`, `frightened` / `fearful`. Other text is passed to the model as written.

______________________________________________________________________

## Delivery modes by family

A [delivery mode](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html#delivery-modes) is a named way of speaking that game code selects with `SetAgentDeliveryMode`. Only three things in the current models carry a sustained mood: a reference clip (Pocket TTS, Chatterbox, Qwen3-TTS), a natural-language clause (Maya1), and the Chatterbox exaggeration scalar. Supertonic 3 and Orpheus have no emotion control, so on those a mode can only change speed, or must stay empty.

| Family                                | Base identity                                           | A delivery mode can set                                                                  | `intensity` (0–1) does                                                                                                   | Cost of switching mode                                                                  | Measured strength                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Supertonic 3                          | `speaker_id` (style `0`–`9`)                            | `speed_scale` only                                                                       | scales `speed_scale`                                                                                                     | none                                                                                    | No emotion. Inline expression tags measured inert.                                                                      |
| Pocket TTS                            | `reference_voice` (default `bria.wav`)                  | `reference_voice`, `speed_scale`                                                         | scales `speed_scale` only; a clip is all or nothing                                                                      | a clip's first use computes an embedding, unless it was prepared when the voice was set | The clip's mood carries over: an angry clip raised pitch, a calm one lowered it.                                        |
| Chatterbox EN / ML / Turbo (internal) | `reference_voice` (variant default)                     | `reference_voice`, `expressiveness` (variants with an exaggeration input), `speed_scale` | lerps `expressiveness` from the profile value to the mode value                                                          | a clip's first use encodes it, unless it was prepared                                   | Exaggeration rated a weak control; the family is a fallback.                                                            |
| Qwen3-TTS 1.7B Base                   | `reference_voice` (required)                            | `reference_voice` only                                                                   | nothing                                                                                                                  | a clip's first use runs the speaker encoder, unless it was prepared                     | The clip's mood carries over. There is no instruction channel: instruction text would be read aloud, so it is rejected. |
| Orpheus 3B FT                         | `speaker_id` (preset `0`–`7`)                           | nothing: modes must be empty                                                             | nothing                                                                                                                  | none                                                                                    | Changing the preset changes who speaks, so it is not a delivery. Most inline tags measured no stronger than a fake tag. |
| Maya1 3B                              | `voice_description`, else `speaker_id` (preset `0`–`1`) | `instruction`                                                                            | picks the clause's intensity word: below `0.34` low, below `0.67` medium, else high (only when `intensity` is below `1`) | none extra; the prompt is re-read on every sentence                                     | `excited` and `angry` clearly raised pitch; `happy` and `sad` on flat text were within noise.                           |

Strength figures come from Tryll's internal listen-back measurements. Treat them as a guide to which modes are worth authoring, not as guarantees.

______________________________________________________________________

## Family support matrix

Sherpa-ONNX v1.13.2 exposes seven TTS families. Tryll accepts two of them. llama.cpp SNAC families are a separate path.

| Family                 | Engine      | Upstream examples           | Status in Tryll  | Why                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------- | ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Supertonic**         | Sherpa-ONNX | Supertonic 3                | ✅ **Supported** | Own tokenizer (`unicode_indexer.bin`); no eSpeak                                                                      |
| **Pocket**             | Sherpa-ONNX | Pocket TTS (Kyutai)         | ✅ **Supported** | SentencePiece vocabulary; no eSpeak                                                                                   |
| **Orpheus**            | llama.cpp   | Orpheus 3B FT               | ✅ **Supported** | SNAC tokens via llama.cpp; shared ONNX decoder                                                                        |
| **Maya1**              | llama.cpp   | Maya1 3B                    | ✅ **Supported** | Same SNAC engine as Orpheus; description + delivery controls                                                          |
| **Qwen3-TTS**          | llama.cpp   | Qwen3-TTS 12Hz 1.7B Base    | ✅ **Supported** | Talker GGUF plus an mmproj codec, run through libmtmd; reference-voice cloning                                        |
| **Kokoro**             | Sherpa-ONNX | Kokoro v0.19, v1.0          | ❌ Unavailable   | Requires eSpeak NG — see below                                                                                        |
| **Kitten**             | Sherpa-ONNX | KittenTTS nano/micro/mini   | ❌ Unavailable   | Requires eSpeak NG — see below                                                                                        |
| **VITS (incl. Piper)** | Sherpa-ONNX | Piper voices, MMS, LJSpeech | ❌ Unavailable   | Piper-style bundles require eSpeak NG. Lexicon-based VITS bundles do not, but the family is not implemented in Tryll. |
| **Matcha**             | Sherpa-ONNX | Matcha-Icefall (en, zh)     | ❌ Unavailable   | English bundles require eSpeak NG. The Chinese lexicon path does not, but the family is not implemented in Tryll.     |
| **ZipVoice**           | Sherpa-ONNX | ZipVoice, ZipVoice-Distill  | ❌ Unavailable   | No eSpeak requirement, but the family is not implemented in Tryll.                                                    |

Note the two distinct reasons for the Sherpa gaps. **Kokoro and Kitten are blocked by licensing** — they cannot be enabled without changing what Tryll redistributes. **VITS, Matcha, and ZipVoice are simply not implemented**; nothing in principle prevents their eSpeak-free bundles from being added later.

______________________________________________________________________

## Why eSpeak-dependent families are unavailable

Sherpa-ONNX performs grapheme-to-phoneme conversion for several families with [eSpeak NG](https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng), which is licensed **GPLv3-or-later**. Linking it into `tryll_server.exe` would make the server a combined work under GPLv3 — and because the server payload is bundled inside your game build, that obligation would follow you, your studio, and your publisher.

Tryll therefore builds Sherpa-ONNX with eSpeak NG **compiled out entirely**. The shipped `sherpa-onnx-c-api.dll` contains no eSpeak code and the payload contains no `espeak-ng-data`. The upside is that nothing in the Tryll server imposes a copyleft obligation on your game. The cost is that any voice whose front-end calls eSpeak cannot run, regardless of how the model's own weights are licensed.

This constraint applies to Sherpa-ONNX families only. llama.cpp SNAC voices do not use eSpeak.

A permissive model license is not enough

KittenTTS is the classic trap: its weights are Apache-2.0, which looks unrestricted, but the model is *trained on eSpeak phoneme IDs* and Sherpa-ONNX's Kitten loader requires a populated `espeak-ng-data` directory. The permissive headline license does not make the runtime dependency go away. The same reasoning excludes Kokoro, whose loader also hard-requires that directory.

______________________________________________________________________

## What happens if you try an unsupported family

A Sherpa-ONNX `models.json` variant whose `tts_family` is anything other than `supertonic` or `pocket` fails when the model is loaded — that is, at `CreateAgent` time for a graph referencing it, not silently at startup. llama.cpp SNAC families (`orpheus`, `maya1`) load when their catalog entries and the shared decoder asset are present.

| `tts_family` value                                                  | Result                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `supertonic`, `pocket`                                              | Loads normally on Sherpa-ONNX                                                                  |
| `orpheus`, `maya1`                                                  | Loads normally on llama.cpp + the shared SNAC decoder                                          |
| `vits`, `piper`, `kokoro`, or empty                                 | Rejected with an explicit eSpeak/GPLv3 message                                                 |
| Any other Sherpa-ONNX value (`kitten`, `matcha`, `zipvoice`, typos) | Rejected as an unknown Sherpa-ONNX family                                                      |
| An unknown llama.cpp value                                          | Rejected: no compiled-in llama.cpp TTS engine serves it (the message lists the known families) |

Those Sherpa-ONNX cases surface as agent-creation failures; see [Error Codes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html). An empty Sherpa-ONNX `tts_family` is rejected rather than defaulting, because the historical default was VITS.

______________________________________________________________________

## Adding your own voice

You can add TTS entries to `models.json` — either a HuggingFace repo or a local path — using the schema in [Model Management](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/model-management.html#variants-entry-fields). For Sherpa-ONNX the constraint is the family, not the source: the bundle must be a Supertonic or Pocket bundle, with the `tts_files` key set that family expects. llama.cpp SNAC voices use `tts_family` `orpheus` or `maya1` plus a shared decoder asset (`dependencies.snac_decoder`).

Sherpa bundles for both supported families are published by the Sherpa-ONNX maintainer on HuggingFace — the shipped ones under [`csukuangfj2`](https://huggingface.co/csukuangfj2), the rest of the zoo mostly under [`csukuangfj`](https://huggingface.co/csukuangfj). A Sherpa bundle from any other family will be rejected at load time even though the catalog entry itself parses.

# String Storage

A **string storage** is a session-owned, named container of strings. It exists to back workflow nodes with fixed text content without baking that content into the graph definition at authoring time.

String storages are **not embedded** and **not indexed**. For vector retrieval, see [embedded string storage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/embedded-string-storage.html).

## Kinds

Every string storage has a **kind** set at creation time; the kind determines what accessors the server exposes to nodes and what validation rules apply.

| Kind       | Description                                 | Key uniqueness           |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `List`     | Ordered sequence of plain strings. No keys. | —                        |
| `Map`      | Ordered sequence of `key → value` pairs.    | Each key must be unique. |
| `Multimap` | Ordered sequence of `key → value` pairs.    | Duplicate keys allowed.  |

All three kinds share a **list view** — the server can iterate every value by position regardless of kind. `Map` and `Multimap` additionally expose a **keyed view** (`FindFirst`, `FindAll`) that is used by nodes which need to look up values by a string key.

Internal storage order for Map and Multimap

The server stores `Map` and `Multimap` entries **sorted by key** (lexicographic, stable within each key group so that duplicate-key values appear in their original insertion order). This makes `FindFirst` and `FindAll` O(log n) binary-search lookups, and guarantees that `FindAll` returns every matching value even when the keys were not grouped at creation time. The list view (`GetByIndex`) reflects this sorted order rather than the original construction order.

Current node support

`CannedResponseNode` and `RegexGuardrailNode` use only the **list view** — they iterate all values in order and are not key-aware. Both nodes accept any kind.

[`IntentToInstructionNode`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/intent-to-instruction.html) uses the **keyed view** (`FindFirst`) and **requires `Map` kind**. It is the primary consumer of Map-kind storages today.

Key-aware `CannedResponse` selection (keyed by a runtime intent label) is planned as future work.

## Lifecycle

**The preferred way to supply string data to a node is a relative file path** set directly on the node's `string_storage` parameter. The server loads the file on demand when the agent is created — no explicit `Create` / `Destroy` is required.

Use explicit `CreateStringStorageRequest` / `DestroyStringStorageRequest` only when you need to share the same in-memory storage across multiple agents, or when you want to supply inline strings rather than a file.

| Step               | Frame                                         | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Lazy load**      | *(none)*                                      | Set `string_storage = "relative/path.txt"` on the node param. The server resolves the path against the process storage root at `CreateAgentRequest` time and loads (or reuses) the storage.                                                                                     |
| **Explicit Pin**   | `CreateStringStorageRequest`                  | Pins the named storage so it is not evicted between agent creations. Server responds with `CreateStringStorageResponse`.                                                                                                                                                        |
| **Use**            | *(referenced by node `string_storage` param)* | Scoped to the [session](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#session). For file-backed storages (lazy or pinned with `file_path`) the param value is the relative file path; for inline storages created with `strings` it is the `name` used at creation. |
| **Explicit Unpin** | `DestroyStringStorageRequest`                 | Demotes a file-backed storage from Pinned to OnDemand (eligible for eviction) or removes a virtual/inline entry. Server responds with `Ack`. Agents that already hold the storage keep it alive — the call only removes the session's named reference.                          |

The session drops every storage it owns on disconnect. See [Lifetime and Ownership → StringStorage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/lifetime-and-ownership.html#stringstorage) for the full ownership model.

## Node param: relative file path (preferred)

Set the node's `string_storage` parameter to a **relative path** under the process storage root:

```
string_storage = "responses/refusal_lines.txt"   // List
string_storage = "intent/instructions.json"       // Map (IntentToInstruction)
```

The path is resolved at `CreateAgentRequest` time against the process storage root, set at server startup (see [Server Configuration → Storage root](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/server-configuration.html#storage-root) for the resolution chain). There is no per-session root. Extension inference:

| Extension  | Inferred kind |
| ---------- | ------------- |
| `.txt`     | List          |
| `.json`    | Map           |
| `.mm.json` | Multimap      |

If the file is outside the root or does not exist, the server returns `3009 StorageOutsideRoot` or `3010 StorageFileNotFound` on `CreateAgentRequest`. If the file kind does not match what the node requires, it returns `3011 StorageKindMismatch`.

## Creation (explicit Pin)

`CreateStringStorageRequest` carries these fields:

| Field       | Type                     | Description                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`      | string                   | Unique name within the session. Required for inline storages. Ignored when `file_path` is set: a file-backed storage is keyed by its path. |
| `kind`      | `StringStorageKind` enum | `List` (0, default), `Map` (1), or `Multimap` (2).                                                                                         |
| `strings`   | `[string]`               | Inline values. For `List`: the strings themselves. For `Map`/`Multimap`: the values, parallel to `keys`.                                   |
| `keys`      | `[string]`               | Inline keys (Map/Multimap only). Must have the same length as `strings`.                                                                   |
| `file_path` | string                   | Relative path to a storage file under the process storage root. Extension → kind inference applies (`.txt` → List, `.json` → Map).         |

Exactly one content source must be provided:

- `strings` alone → **List** inline (virtual/named registration).
- `strings` + `keys` → **Map** or **Multimap** inline (virtual/named).
- `file_path` → file-based (Pins the loaded storage against eviction).

Old clients that do not set `kind` default to `List` and keep working without any changes.

### File format — List (`.txt`)

UTF-8 text, one value per line. Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored:

```
# Lines starting with # are comments.
# Blank lines are also ignored.

I can't help with that.
I can't assist with that request.
```

### File format — Map / Multimap (`.json`)

A JSON **array** of objects with `id` (key) and `text` (value) fields. This is the same on-disk shape used by knowledge-base records; a `metadata` field is accepted but ignored in this context.

```
[
  {"id": "greet_friendly", "text": "Hello there, traveller!"},
  {"id": "greet_friendly", "text": "Well met!"},
  {"id": "greet_hostile",  "text": "What do you want?"}
]
```

Duplicate `id` values are rejected for `Map` kind and accepted for `Multimap` kind.

Note

Relative paths in `file_path` (and in the node `string_storage` param) are resolved against the **process storage root** — CLI `--storage-root`, config `storage_root`, or the mode default (Client Dev: `<Project>/TryllStorage/`). Protocol v24 removed per-session `storage_data_folder`. Never use absolute paths; they are rejected with `3009 StorageOutsideRoot`.

## Server defaults

If a canned-response or guardrail node is created with **no** `string_storage` param and an empty `inline_strings` list, the server falls back to a file configured in [`server-config.json`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/server-configuration.html):

- `default_canned_responses_path` — default responses (List kind).
- `default_guardrail_patterns_path` — default patterns (List kind, regex).

Both files are plain `.txt` (List kind). There are no JSON defaults.

## Resolution order

A canned-response or guardrail node resolves its string source in this order:

1. **Named storage** — `string_storage` param set → look up in the session's storage manager.
1. **Inline strings** — `inline_strings` non-empty → use as-is.
1. **Server default** — load from the configured default file.

## Minimum working examples

```
client.create_string_storage(
    name="refusal_lines",
    strings=[
        "I can't help with that.",
        "That's outside what I can do.",
    ],
)
# Reference "refusal_lines" from a CannedResponse node
# via the `string_storage` param.
```

```
client.CreateStringStorage("refusal_lines", {
    "I can't help with that.",
    "That's outside what I can do.",
});
```

```
auto* Subsystem = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UTryllSubsystem>();
Subsystem->RequestCreateStringStorage(
    TEXT("refusal_lines"),
    { TEXT("I can't help with that."),
      TEXT("That's outside what I can do.") });
```

```
client.create_keyed_string_storage(
    name="intent_instructions",
    keys=["greet", "farewell"],
    values=["Say hello warmly.", "Say goodbye politely."],
    kind=StringStorageKind.Map,
)
```

```
client.CreateStringStorageKeyed(
    "intent_instructions",
    {"greet", "farewell"},
    {"Say hello warmly.", "Say goodbye politely."},
    ::Tryll::StringStorageKind_Map);
```

```
auto* Subsystem = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UTryllSubsystem>();
Subsystem->RequestCreateStringStorageKeyed(
    TEXT("intent_instructions"),
    { TEXT("greet"), TEXT("farewell") },
    { TEXT("Say hello warmly."), TEXT("Say goodbye politely.") },
    1 /* Map */);
```

```
await client.RequestCreateKeyedStringStorageAsync(
    "intent_instructions",
    new List<string> { "greet", "farewell" },
    new List<string> { "Say hello warmly.", "Say goodbye politely." },
    Tryll.StringStorageKind.Map);
```

## Errors

| Code                                                                                       | Cause                                                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`3009`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent)          | `string_storage` param path escapes the storage root (absolute path or `..` traversal). Fix: use a relative path.                               |
| [`3010`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent)          | `string_storage` param path resolves inside the root but the file is absent. Fix: place the file under the process storage root.                |
| [`3011`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#3xxx-agent)          | `string_storage` param file kind does not match what the node requires (e.g. `.txt` for `IntentToInstruction` which requires Map).              |
| [`7001`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#7xxx-string-storage) | Name empty, malformed, or reserved.                                                                                                             |
| [`7002`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#7xxx-string-storage) | A storage with this name already exists in the session.                                                                                         |
| [`7003`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#7xxx-string-storage) | Content rejected: unreadable file, empty array, bad format, duplicate key in Map, size mismatch between `keys` and `strings`.                   |
| [`7004`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#7xxx-string-storage) | Inline virtual name shadows an existing real file under the storage root. Choose a name that does not match any filename in the storage folder. |

## Client bindings

|            | List (inline)                                    | List (file)                                           | Map / Multimap (inline)                                          | Map / Multimap (file)                                       |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **C++**    | `CreateStringStorage(name, strings)`             | `CreateStringStorageFromFile(name, path)`             | `CreateStringStorageKeyed(name, keys, values, kind)`             | `CreateStringStorageFromFile(name, path, kind)`             |
| **Python** | `create_string_storage(name, strings=…)`         | `create_string_storage(name, file_path=…)`            | `create_keyed_string_storage(name, keys, values, kind)`          | `create_string_storage(name, file_path=…, kind=…)`          |
| **Unreal** | `RequestCreateStringStorage(Name, Strings)`      | `RequestCreateStringStorageFromFile(Name, Path)`      | `RequestCreateStringStorageKeyed(Name, Keys, Values, Kind)`      | `RequestCreateStringStorageFromFile(Name, Path, Kind)`      |
| **Unity**  | `RequestCreateStringStorageAsync(name, strings)` | `RequestCreateStringStorageFromFileAsync(name, path)` | `RequestCreateKeyedStringStorageAsync(name, keys, values, kind)` | `RequestCreateStringStorageFromFileAsync(name, path, kind)` |

All methods complete asynchronously (C++: blocking with timeout; Python: blocking; Unreal/Unity: `Task`/callback).\
The `kind` parameter for Unreal uses `uint8` ordinals: `0` = `List`, `1` = `Map`, `2` = `Multimap`.\
For C++ and Python, use the typed `::Tryll::StringStorageKind_Map` / `StringStorageKind.Map` constants.

# Embedded String Storage

An **embedded string storage** is a session-owned, named, vector-indexed container of text chunks. It is the backing store for every [Retrieve node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve.html) in a [graph](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#graph) — the building block of [RAG](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#rag) in Tryll.

Under the hood, each storage holds:

1. A list of **records** — `{ id, text }` pairs, optionally with metadata.
1. A precomputed [embedding](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#embedding) per record.
1. An [HNSW](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#hnsw) index over those embeddings, tuned for cosine distance.
1. An in-process **Okapi BM25** index over record text (persisted as a `.bm25` sidecar on Path A), used by [Retrieve](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve.html) in `Lexical` / `Hybrid` modes. Tokenization is Unicode-aware (casefold + letter/number split via utf8proc); sidecar **format version 2** — older ASCII-casefold sidecars are rebuilt on next load.

Dense retrieval uses embedding similarity. Lexical / Hybrid modes add BM25 (and RRF fusion for Hybrid). For plain substring / regex / exact-match over non-embedded lists, see [string storage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/string-storage.html).

## Node param: relative file path (preferred)

Set the node's `embedded_string_storage` parameter to a **relative path** under the process storage root:

```
embedded_string_storage = "rag/adventure_quests.json"
```

The path is resolved at `CreateAgentRequest` time against the process storage root, set at server startup (see [Server Configuration → Storage root](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/server-configuration.html#storage-root)). There is no per-session root; a path that resolves outside it is rejected with `3009 StorageOutsideRoot`. The server loads the KB config file, builds or reuses a cached HNSW index, and Pins the entry so it survives eviction for the lifetime of the agent.

## Creation paths (explicit Pin)

`CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest` supports two construction paths. Exactly one is used per request.

| Path                | Trigger             | What the server does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A** (file-backed) | `config_path` set   | Relative path resolved against the process storage root. Loads the KB config JSON, resolves `records_file` and optional `index_file` / `bm25_file` relative to the config's directory, builds or loads the HNSW + BM25 indexes, and Pins the entry. |
| **B** (inline)      | `strings` non-empty | Embeds every string with `embedding_model` and builds an in-memory HNSW index. Registered as a virtual entry under `name`.                                                                                                                          |

`embedding_model` is **required** for Path B (inline strings). For Path A (file-backed), the model is taken from the KB config file; the wire `embedding_model` field is ignored.

### Path A — `config_path`

The config is a UTF-8 JSON file with this shape:

```
{
    "version": 1,
    "embedding_model": "All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
    "records_file": "adventure_quests.kb.json",
    "index_file": "adventure_quests.kb.usearch",
    "bm25_file": "adventure_quests.kb.bm25",
    "bm25_tokenizer": "basic",
    "fields": [
        { "name": "min_level",         "type": "int",         "default": 0      },
        { "name": "character_class",   "type": "string",      "optional": true  },
        { "name": "character_classes", "type": "set<string>", "optional": true  }
    ]
}
```

| Field             | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `version`         | int    | No       | Schema version. Currently `1`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `embedding_model` | string | Yes      | Catalog name of the embedding model. Must exist in `models.json` with `"model_type": "embedding"`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `records_file`    | string | Yes      | Relative path (from the config file's directory) to the records JSON.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `index_file`      | string | No       | Relative path to a pre-built `*.usearch` HNSW index. If absent, the server builds the index at load time from the records and their embeddings.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `bm25_file`       | string | No       | Relative path to a persisted BM25 sidecar. If omitted and `index_file` is set, defaults to the same stem with a `.bm25` extension (e.g. `adventure_quests.kb.usearch` → `adventure_quests.kb.bm25`). First load **builds and writes** the sidecar; later loads **reuse** it until the records file is newer, or format / tokenizer / doc-count mismatch forces a rebuild. |
| `bm25_tokenizer`  | string | No       | `"basic"` (default) or `"enhanced"`. Both modes Unicode-casefold via utf8proc, then split on non-letter/non-number. `"enhanced"` additionally drops a small English stopword set and applies a trivial suffix strip. Stored in the sidecar header; changing it forces a rebuild. Format version **2** (utf8proc) rebuilds any version-1 ASCII sidecar automatically.      |
| `fields`          | array  | No       | Typed metadata schema — field declarations for filterable record metadata. When present, each record's `metadata` object is validated against it at load time. See [Metadata schema](#metadata-schema).                                                                                                                                                                   |

The **records file** (`*.kb.json` by convention) is a JSON array of objects:

```
[
    {
        "id":   "ai_storytellers_1",
        "text": "The AI storyteller is the main mechanism used to ...",
        "metadata": { "source": "…", "link": "…" }
    },
    {
        "id":   "ai_storytellers_2",
        "text": "…"
    }
]
```

Per record:

| Field      | Type   | Required | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---------- | ------ | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`       | string | Yes      | Stable identifier; returned on retrieval so clients can map back to the source.                                                                                                                                                        |
| `text`     | string | Yes      | The chunk text, already segmented to a size that fits within the embedding model's context window.                                                                                                                                     |
| `metadata` | object | No       | Optional typed metadata object. When the config declares a `fields` schema, each record's metadata is validated and stored in typed slots used by the Retrieve node's `filter` predicate. Fields not listed in the schema are ignored. |

If an `index_file` is present, its dimension must match `embedding_model`'s output dimension; a mismatch is rejected with error `8003` `InvalidEmbeddedStringStorageData`.

## Metadata schema

When a config includes a `fields` array, the server validates every record's `metadata` object against it at load time and stores the values in typed per-field slots. Those slots are what the Retrieve node's [`filter` predicate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve-filter-grammar.html) compares against during vector search — the filter compiler resolves field names to slot indices once at compile time, so no string lookups happen on the hot path.

### Field declarations

Each entry in `fields` declares one filterable field:

| Key          | Required                  | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | Yes                       | Field identifier used in records and in filter references (`{"knowledge": "<name>"}`).                                    |
| `type`       | Yes                       | One of `int`, `float`, `string`, `bool`, `set<string>`.                                                                   |
| `default`    | Exclusive with `optional` | Value applied when a record omits this field. Must be coercible to `type`.                                                |
| `optional`   | Exclusive with `default`  | `true` — missing field is allowed; filters referencing it on a record where it is absent evaluate to `false`.             |
| `filterable` | No (default `true`)       | If `false`, the field is loaded but cannot be referenced in filters. Useful for display-only fields such as `page_title`. |

Exactly one of `default` or `optional: true` must be present — a field that is neither is a load-time error.

### Supported types

| Type          | JSON value in records | Notes                                                                  |
| ------------- | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `int`         | number (integer)      | Stored as `int64`.                                                     |
| `float`       | number                | Stored as `double`. `int`↔`float` promotion is allowed in comparisons. |
| `string`      | string                |                                                                        |
| `bool`        | `true` / `false`      |                                                                        |
| `set<string>` | array of strings      | Stored sorted and deduplicated. Used as the `haystack` of an `in` op.  |

### Missing-field semantics

When a field is declared `optional: true` and a record omits it, every comparison or `in` operation that references that field on that record evaluates to **false**. The field is not treated as "no restriction" — filter authors who want an unrestricted fallback should encode it explicitly with `or` and a separate boolean gating field.

### Example

```
{
    "version": 1,
    "embedding_model": "All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
    "records_file": "adventure_quests.kb.json",
    "index_file":   "adventure_quests.kb.usearch",
    "fields": [
        { "name": "topic",             "type": "string",      "default": ""       },
        { "name": "min_level",         "type": "int",         "default": 0        },
        { "name": "tier",              "type": "string",      "default": "common" },
        { "name": "character_class",   "type": "string",      "optional": true    },
        { "name": "character_classes", "type": "set<string>", "optional": true    },
        { "name": "quest_reached",     "type": "string",      "optional": true    }
    ]
}
```

A record that uses this schema might look like:

```
{
    "id":   "warrior_combat_intro",
    "text": "The sword-and-shield style favoured by Aldhaven warriors …",
    "metadata": {
        "topic":             "Combat",
        "min_level":         1,
        "character_classes": ["warrior", "paladin"]
    }
}
```

`topic`, `min_level`, and `tier` use defaults when absent. `character_class`, `character_classes`, and `quest_reached` are optional and will evaluate to `false` in any filter that references them on a record that omits them.

See [Retrieve filter grammar](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve-filter-grammar.html) for the full JSON predicate syntax that queries these fields.

### Path B — inline `strings`

For programmatic small-scale use, the client sends strings directly:

| Field             | Type       | Required | Description                                                        |
| ----------------- | ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `name`            | string     | Yes      | Unique name within the session.                                    |
| `strings`         | `[string]` | Yes      | The chunks. The server assigns sequential `id`s (`"0"`, `"1"`, …). |
| `embedding_model` | string     | Yes      | Catalog name of the embedding model.                               |

The server embeds every string at creation time and builds the index in memory. Nothing is written to disk; the storage is gone once the session ends.

## Lifecycle

**The preferred approach is a relative file path on the node param** — no explicit `Create` / `Destroy` is needed. The server caches the loaded index and Pins it when the agent is created; the cache entry reverts to OnDemand (eligible for eviction) when the agent is destroyed.

Use explicit `CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest` / `DestroyEmbeddedStringStorageRequest` only when you need to share the same index across multiple agents or supply inline strings (Path B).

| Step               | Frame                                                           | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Lazy load**      | *(none)*                                                        | Set `embedded_string_storage = "relative/kb.json"` on the node param. The server resolves, loads, and Pins the index at `CreateAgentRequest` time.                                                                      |
| **Explicit Pin**   | `CreateEmbeddedStringStorageRequest`                            | Pins the storage so it persists beyond a single agent creation. Server responds with `CreateEmbeddedStringStorageResponse` carrying `record_count` and `embedding_dim`.                                                 |
| **Use**            | *(referenced by Retrieve node `embedded_string_storage` param)* | Scoped to the [session](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#session). For a Path A storage the param value is the relative `config_path`; for a Path B storage it is the `name` used at creation. |
| **Explicit Unpin** | `DestroyEmbeddedStringStorageRequest`                           | For file-backed (Path A) entries: demotes from Pinned to OnDemand, eligible for eviction once no agent holds it. For virtual (Path B) entries: removes the named entry. Server responds with `Ack`.                     |

See [Lifetime and Ownership → EmbeddedStringStorage](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/lifetime-and-ownership.html#embeddedstringstorage) for the full ownership model and the separation between the on-disk index cache and the in-memory index object.

## Consumption by Retrieve

A [Retrieve node](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/retrieve.html) names the storage via its `embedded_string_storage` param. Per turn, the node:

1. Embeds the user's message with the embedding model recorded in the KB config file referenced by `embedded_string_storage`.
1. Queries the storage's HNSW index for the `top_k` closest records by cosine distance. If a `filter` is set on the node, each candidate record's metadata is evaluated against the compiled predicate during the search; records that do not match are excluded before `top_k` is applied.
1. Drops results whose distance exceeds `threshold`.
1. Emits one [knowledge component](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#knowledge-component) per surviving record onto the current [interaction](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#interaction).

How those components appear in the [prompt](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/glossary.html#prompt) is controlled by the downstream `Generate` node's `template` (Mustache) and `placement` params — see [Use Mustache Templates](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-mustache-templates.html).

## Validation and errors

The server validates at creation time:

- Exactly one of `config_path` / `strings` must be set.
- Path B: the wire `embedding_model` must be in the catalog with `"model_type": "embedding"`.
- Path A: the KB config's `embedding_model` must be in the catalog with `"model_type": "embedding"`.
- Path A: `records_file` must exist, parse, and be non-empty.
- Path A with `index_file`: the index must load and its dimension must match the embedding model.
- Path B: `strings` must be non-empty.

| Code                                                                                                | Cause                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`8001`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#8xxx-embedded-string-storage) | Name empty, malformed, or reserved.                                                                                              |
| [`8002`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#8xxx-embedded-string-storage) | A storage with this name already exists in the session.                                                                          |
| [`8003`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html#8xxx-embedded-string-storage) | Content rejected: missing / corrupt config or records, empty inline array, unknown embedding model, or index-dimension mismatch. |

## Minimum working example

```
# Path B (inline)
client.create_embedded_string_storage(
    name="aquarium_kb",
    strings=[
        "Neon tetras thrive in soft, slightly acidic water.",
        "Goldfish are cold-water fish and should not share a tank with tropicals.",
    ],
    embedding_model="All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
)

# Path A (file-backed) — relative path resolved against the process storage root
client.create_embedded_string_storage(
    name="rimworld_kb",
    config_path="rag/rimworld.json",
    embedding_model="All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)",
)
```

```
// Path B (inline)
client.CreateEmbeddedStringStorageFromStrings(
    "aquarium_kb",
    {
        "Neon tetras thrive in soft, slightly acidic water.",
        "Goldfish are cold-water fish and should not share a tank with tropicals.",
    },
    "All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)");

// Path A (file-backed) — relative path resolved against the process storage root
auto info = client.CreateEmbeddedStringStorage(
    "rimworld_kb",
    "rag/rimworld.json",
    /*embeddingModel=*/"All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)");
```

```
auto* subsystem = GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UTryllSubsystem>();

// Path B (inline) — requires EmbeddingModel.
subsystem->RequestCreateEmbeddedStringStorageFromStrings(
    TEXT("aquarium_kb"),
    { TEXT("Neon tetras thrive in soft, slightly acidic water."),
      TEXT("Goldfish are cold-water fish and should not share a tank with tropicals.") },
    TEXT("All-MiniLM-L6-v2 (Q4_K_M)"));

// Path A (file-backed). Relative path; model comes from the KB config.
subsystem->RequestCreateEmbeddedStringStorage(
    TEXT("rimworld_kb"),
    TEXT("rag/rimworld.json"));

// Bind OnCreateEmbeddedStringStorageComplete(Name, RecordCount, bSuccess)
// to continue once the index is built.
```

See the full workflow in [How to create a simple RAG assistant](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/create-simple-rag-assistant.html).

## Client bindings

- **C++:** `Tryll::Client::TryllClient::CreateEmbeddedStringStorage` (file config) / `CreateEmbeddedStringStorageFromStrings` (inline) — `TryllClient.h`
- **Python:** `tryll_client.TryllClient.create_embedded_string_storage` (pass either `config_path=…` or `strings=…`) — `client.py`
- **Unreal:** `UTryllSubsystem::RequestCreateEmbeddedStringStorage` — `TryllSubsystem.h`
