- **Sentence splitting understands more scripts.** CJK, Devanagari, Arabic, Urdu and Ethiopic sentence ends close a chunk without a following space, and closing quotes stay with their sentence. `…` counts as a full stop. `min_sentence_chars` is now a width: a CJK character counts as two, so the default of 12 is about six CJK characters. A number such as `3.14` is no longer split after the `3.`. Text that never ends a sentence is cut at a 16 KiB cap, with a warning.
- **`first_chunk_max_chars` on `GenerateAndSpeak` and `Speak`.** Default `0` (off). When set, only the first chunk may also end at a comma, semicolon, colon or em dash, and it is cut at the next space once it reaches that width. It never cuts before 5 words or `min_sentence_chars`. `48` reduced the model-side wait before the first audio by about 40% in our measurements. Listen to it with your own voice first, because a clause can end on a falling tone. See [Speak](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/speak.html) and [Generate and Speak](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate-and-speak.html).
- **Raw PCM for your own audio pipeline.** `TryllSpeaker.OnTtsPcm` (Unity) and `UTryllSpeakerComponent::OnTtsPcm` (Unreal) hand you every decoded buffer, for example to feed your own spatializer. The Unity speaker also exposes `OnTtsFormat`, `ConsumedSamples` and `QueuedSamples`. See [TryllSpeaker](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-speaker.html).
- **Unity speaker fixes.** A `TryllAgentComponent` with an empty Speaker slot now reuses the `TryllSpeaker` already on the GameObject instead of adding a second one, which also left a lip-sync component following a silent speaker. A speaker that is disabled and re-enabled now plays again.
- **`speed` is checked the same way at creation and at runtime.** `ChangeAgentParam` now enforces the 0.1–3.0 range too, as `CreateAgent` already did.

## Voice input

- **Your client sends the voice turn.** The server now only transcribes. On `UtteranceFinal`, send the text yourself with `SendText`, `send_message_async`, or the agent component's `SendMessage`. Unity and Unreal voice components do this for you when a target agent is set, and drop the final if that agent already has a turn in flight. In Python, use `send_message_async` from the transcript callback, because the blocking `send_message` deadlocks on the reader thread. See [Use voice input](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-voice-input.html).
- **Hotword biasing you can switch per model.** The Model Manager has a **Hotword biasing** control (Default / Off / On) on STT models. In code, pass `hotword_hints` (Python) or `placementHints` with `.hotwords` (C++) to `CreateSession`. The shipped catalog turns biasing on for Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3.
- **Better lexicons.** Write plain words, one phrase per line. Append `:<score>` to boost a single phrase. Pretokenized lexicons still work. The default `hotwordsScore` stays `1.5`, and the guide's recommended ranges moved up. Transducer and streaming Zipformer models support hotwords, but CTC-family models do not. An unsupported model now logs a warning at voice-input creation instead of ignoring the lexicon silently. See [Bias voice input with hotwords](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-voice-input-hotwords.html).
- **Unity voice component sets hotwords.** `TryllVoiceInputComponent` gains `hotwordsStoragePath` (a Storage Data Folder file picker; leave it empty to disable) and `hotwordsScore`. See [TryllVoiceInputComponent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-voice-input-component.html).

## Intent classification

- **`ClassifyIntentLLM` takes an `intents` array.** Author id/prompt pairs as entries (`ClassifyIntentEntry` in Python, `TryllClassifyIntentEntry` in Unity, `FTryllClassifyIntentEntry` in Unreal), so a description can contain a comma. The comma-separated `intents_ids` / `intents_prompt` pair is **deprecated** and kept for one release. If `intents` is empty, the node falls back to it. Setting both is a graph-creation error. Unreal binary assets were not migrated, so copy the values out of the inspector to use the array. See [Classify Intent (LLM)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent-llm.html).
- **The classifier prompt is checked up front.** `system_prompt` must be a Mustache template that parses and references `{{intents_block}}`. Otherwise `CreateAgent` and `ChangeAgentParam` fail, where previously the template was sent anyway and classification quietly broke. `{{letters}}` is now optional. See [Design an intent-classifier prompt](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/design-an-intent-classifier-prompt.html).

## Tool calling

- **Tool Call diagnostics say why a parse failed.** When `output.parse_fallback` is true, `output.parse_failure` reports whether the model attempted a call and got the syntax wrong (`malformed_call`), answered in prose (`no_call`), or used a chat template that declares no call marker to check against (`unclassified`). `output.parse_error` gives the parser's reason and the byte where it stopped. The Unity and Unreal turn inspectors show both under the parse-fallback chip. See [Tool Call diagnostics](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/tool-call.html#diagnostics).
- **[Fix tool-call text in answers](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/fix-tool-call-text-in-answers.html).** What to check when a reply shows raw tool-call markup such as `<|tool_call>…` instead of dialogue: a speech node told to call a tool on a turn that skipped `ToolCall`, an unparsed call sent under `mode = call_or_answer`, or leaked replies replaying from history.
- **Unity: async tool handlers.** `RegisterTool` on `TryllAgent` / `TryllAgentComponent` accepts `Func<TryllToolCall, Task<string>>`. The paused batch is held until every handler completes on the main thread, and results that already succeeded are kept across a retry. Synchronous handlers are unaffected.
- **Dialog Lab treats a tool-call mismatch as a check failure.** A missing, unexpected or wrong-name call now completes the turn as an amber **CheckFail** with its diagnostics, and the rest of the script keeps running. See [Test tool calls in Chat and the Lab](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/test-tool-calls-in-editor.html).

## Retrieval

- **[Query rewriting and HyDE for RAG](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/query-rewriting-for-rag.html).** A second rewrite recipe writes a short hypothetical passage instead of a keyword query (HyDE). It works better when your knowledge base stores statements rather than questions. The page includes a table for choosing between the two recipes by how your chunks are written, and advice on re-checking `threshold` and keeping a `Keywords:` line for Hybrid retrieval.

## Models and catalogs

- **User model catalog.** Set **Project Settings → Tryll Client → Custom Models → Catalog** (Unity) or **Project Settings → Plugins → Tryll Client → Models** (Unreal) to a JSON file inside the project. You can also call `TrySetUserModelsCatalogPath` / `SetUserModelsCatalogPath` before the server launches. Setting it while an auto-launched server is running restarts that server. A packaged game stages the file under `Server/data/user-catalog/`, with relative chat templates beside it. A standalone server takes `user_models_catalog_path` / `--user-models-path` or a `models.d` folder (`--user-models-dir`), and `tryll_server --check-catalogs` validates them. A broken user file is skipped, and a duplicate name loses to the shipped entry. See [Use your own local model](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-your-own-local-model.html) and [Model Management](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/model-management.html#modelsjson).
- **Runtime model management is explicit.** When a model must be acquired: call `RequestDownloadModel`, wait for a successful `OnDownloadComplete`, then call `RequestLoadModel`. Call `RequestLoadModel` alone to pin a model that is already staged, or create the agent and let the server load on demand. See [Pin and unpin models](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/pin-and-unpin-models.html).
- **A broken `models.json` stops the server.** A missing file, a parse error, or the retired `device_preference` key now exits the server with an error, the same way a broken `server-config.json` already did. Before, it logged a warning and served an empty catalog.

## Server, storage and deployment

- **Deployment modes.** `--mode` (or the `mode` key) selects `tryll-dev`, `client-dev` or `client-prod`. The mode sets the default roots, the log file, whether models can be downloaded, and which developer features run. The monitor, debug commands and STT debug dumps work only in Tryll Dev. Client Dev and Client Prod refuse to start without a config file. Unity and Unreal auto-launch the server in Client Dev. See [Run the Tryll server](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/run-the-tryll-server.html) and [Server configuration](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/server-configuration.html#deployment-mode).
- **One storage root per process.** Relative storage paths resolve against `--storage-root` / `storage_root`, or the mode's default. Models and logs follow `--models-root` / `models_root` and `--log-dir` / `logs_dir`. The session no longer carries a storage folder, and `ConnectionReady` reports the server's `mode`.
- **`TryllStorage` in Unity and Unreal.** Storage defaults to `<Project>/TryllStorage/`, outside the engine asset folders. Unity copies it into `StreamingAssets/Tryll/` in the build output. Unreal stages it next to the packaged project, so you no longer need **Additional Non-Asset Directories to Copy**. See [Ship storage folders for builds](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/ship-storage-folders-for-builds.html).
- **Client Dev logs per project.** Each run writes one log file under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Tryll\projects\<project-key>\logs\`, not inside the plugin package. The deployment mode, not `log_mode`, now picks the file name: a per-run `tryll_<timestamp>.log` in Tryll Dev and Client Dev, a rotating `tryll.log` in Client Prod. Crash dumps always go to the logs folder.
- **Usage telemetry in Client Dev.** Host ID, hardware inventory and session-started events always send in Client Dev. Activity telemetry is a separate lane (`activity_enabled`, default `true`). See [Telemetry](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/telemetry.html).

## Client APIs

- **Events per agent.** Unity `TryllAgent` / `TryllAgentComponent` and Unreal `UTryllAgentComponent` raise tool-call, intent, pause and generic node events for that agent only, with the payload alone (`ToolCallDetailed`, `IntentClassified`, `IntentLlmClassified`, `Paused`, `NodeEvent` and the tool-call variants in Unity, and their `On…` counterparts in Unreal). Bind these when you care about one NPC. The session events remain the all-agents surface. A typed listener suppresses only its own scope's generic `NodeEvent`. See [TryllAgentComponent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-agent-component.html) and the [Blueprint catalog](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unreal/blueprint-catalog.html).
- **Unity: code-created agents receive their own answers.** `TryllAgent` has public `SetOnAnswerText`, `SetOnTurnComplete`, `SetOnError`, `SetOnTtsAudioFormat` and `SetOnTtsAudio`, matching C++, Unreal and Python. Register them before `SendMessage`, and pass `null` to clear. `TryllSpeaker.HandleFormat` / `HandleAudio` are public, so you can wire playback without a component. See [TryllAgent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/index.html#tryllagent).
- **Unity and Unreal error enums list every server code.** `TryllErrorCode` / `ETryllErrorCode` are now generated from the server's list, so new codes appear without a client release lagging behind.
- **Unity/Unreal: an oversized request fails on its own.** A command too large to send now fails that request with `5003 FrameTooLarge` (or `3021 DialogSnapshotTooLarge` for a dialog import), and the connection stays up.
- **Unity/Unreal: an empty send is not a turn.** `SendMessage("")` does nothing, so a leftover empty string never reaches the server as a malformed request.
- **Unreal plugin builds on UE 5.8 as well as 5.7.** Play-in-Editor still waits for the model check and resumes when it passes.
- **Play-in-Editor pause warning.** If no `OnPaused` is bound, a pause nothing can resume now logs its warning in PIE, and the subsystem's `OnNodeEvent` receives `paused` events. Previously the editor's own subscription hid both.

## Agentic coding

- **[Agentic coding with Tryll](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/agentic-coding-with-tryll.html).** How to have an AI coding agent build Tryll agents: `AGENTS.md`, and prompt advice from real runs.
- **Tryll MCP plugin (Unreal 5.8).** A separate `TryllMCP` plugin, off by default, gives an AI coding agent four tools through the Unreal editor's MCP server: describe node types, and validate, write and read a whole workflow asset. It requires Epic's experimental Model Context Protocol and Toolset Registry plugins.

## Editor

- **Chat voice input is one menu.** **Off**, **Chat** (Chat owns speech-to-text) or **Actor component**. Unity drives the scene `TryllVoiceInputComponent` in Play Mode. Unreal copies that component's STT model, VAD and hotwords into Chat's own handle, so it works without PIE. Unity push-to-talk with a Voice Component no longer sticks, and a quick release no longer starts the microphone after the utterance has ended. See [Test an agent in the editor](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/test-agent-in-editor.html).
- **One status bar and banner across every window.** Chat, Model Manager, Memory, Dialog Lab, Agent Log and Knowledge show connection state the same way. A dropped connection or failed session offers **Retry**. Failed model loads, unloads, downloads and Dialog Lab import errors appear on an inline banner. Destructive confirms stay as dialogs.
- **Windows follow the host editor theme**, including Unity's light skin. Chat bubbles match Dialog Lab, and status colours are the same in every window.
- **Layouts persist.** Inspector and list widths, the Model Manager columns (now resizable), and the Unity Dialog Lab and Agent Log settings survive an editor restart and stay with the project. Collapsing an inspector no longer saves a zero width or leaves a gap.
- **Chat and Agent Log follow the tail only when you are near the bottom**, so scrolling up mid-stream no longer jumps back on every token.
- **Model Manager opens even when registered models are missing.** It lists the catalog first, then prompts you to download.
- **Fixes.** Restoring several Tryll windows at once no longer wedges Chat on a duplicate session. The Unity Memory and Agent Log windows no longer throw on editor start. Entering Play in Unity with an editor window connected now logs a reconnect warning instead of a socket-thread crash. Dialog Lab per-variant agents keep their assignment across a scene unload. Unreal icons that rendered as empty boxes are fixed.
- **The Unreal `TryllUnrealDemo` project packages again after the editor saves it.** Its `.uproject` description had a non-ASCII dash. When the editor rewrote the file, which it does on its own or on an engine-version switch, it saved it as UTF-16. UnrealBuildTool then failed on byte 0 with `JsonReaderException: '0xFF' is an invalid start of a value`, and packaging and project-file generation both stopped. The descriptor is now ASCII-only. A copy from an earlier release that already shows this error needs re-saving as UTF-8 without a BOM, in any text editor. A version-switch copy can also be left with an engine GUID in `EngineAssociation`; set it back to your version, such as `"5.8"`. Keep your own `.uproject` and `.uplugin` text ASCII-only for the same reason.

## Documentation

- **[Tryll in Ten Minutes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/tryll-in-ten-minutes.html)** is the new starting point: what Tryll is, why it runs on the player's machine, agents as workflows, the building blocks, and how a team works with it. [Architecture at a Glance](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/architecture-at-a-glance.html) becomes the engineer's view.
- **Docs are versioned.** Each minor release is published under `/vX.Y/` with a version switcher. The plugin version is in `package.json`, the `.uplugin`, or `AGENTS.md`.
- **Samples compile against the current API.** Every `CreateSession` sample is free of the engine arguments that v0.7.0 removed, and the C++, Python, Unity and Unreal graph samples use the real builder and parameter types.
- **Corrections that may change how you integrate.** The code did not change in these cases; the earlier docs were wrong:
  - `Speak` voices its `input` slot, which defaults to `user_message`. It does not voice the last answer. Behind a `Generate`, set `input` to that node's output.
  - A `ToolCall` pause times out after **2000 ms** by default, inherited from the shipped `workflow.tool_call_pause_timeout_ms`, and the turn ends with `PauseTimedOut`. Set `pause_timeout_ms` if your tool handlers are slow.
  - An exit that names a missing node fails with `3003 GraphCompilationFailed`, not `3008`. An empty exit is valid and ends the turn.
  - An unknown or missing model in a graph fails `CreateAgent` with `3003`, not `4002`. A second `SendMessage` during a live turn returns `3004 AgentBusy`.
  - `tts_voice` is rejected, not ignored, on every voice except Pocket TTS.
  - Unloading a model drops its pin straight away, but the model stays resident until every agent using it is destroyed.
  - A streamed answer ends with an empty terminator frame (`is_final = true`, `text = ""`), so a handler that prints the final chunk prints an empty line.
  - `duration_s` in turn diagnostics includes paused time. Subtract `paused_duration_s` to get running time.
  - The Python client needs Python 3.11 or later.

## Breaking changes and behavior changes

- **The schema changed — rebuild every client.** Voice input, the TTS and classifier nodes, the new `Summarize`, `WriteToMemory` and lip-sync messages, mutable knowledge bases, and session setup all changed shape. Rebuild your integration against the new schema and upgrade both ends together. Mismatched peers fail at connect: the client rejects the server's protocol version with `5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch`. See [Wire Protocol](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html#versioning).
- **Packaged games are not yet shippable to players.** Unity and Unreal player builds still launch the server in Client Dev until a Client Prod build exists, and Client Dev always sends usage telemetry (see below). Do not ship those builds to end users.
- **Client Dev usage telemetry cannot be turned off.** `telemetry.enabled = false` does not stop the usage lane in Client Dev. The server keeps it on and warns. True opt-out exists only in Tryll Dev (`--disable-telemetry`, or `TRYLL_SERVER_MODE=tryll-dev` for an auto-launched server). **`include_user_content` now defaults to `true` (was `false`).** It applies only to activity events, so set it to `false` if slot text and tool arguments must not leave the machine. See [Telemetry](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/telemetry.html).
- **Voice turns are client-sent.** `BeginUtterance` no longer takes an agent id, and the server no longer starts a turn from a transcript. Send `UtteranceFinal` text yourself (see [Voice input](#voice-input)). A busy rejection is now an `AgentBusy` error only, with no `TurnComplete` after it.
- **`vad_min_silence_ms` defaults to 1000 (was 500).** This applies when the field is omitted, and in Unity `TryllVoiceInputComponent.vadMinSilenceMs`. Speech now needs a longer pause before a segment closes. Set it back to 500 if you depended on the faster cut.
- **A lexicon on a model with hotword biasing off is refused** with `4106 HotwordBiasDisabled` instead of being ignored. CTC-family STT models are no longer described as supporting hotwords.
- **Stricter node parameters.** Schema ranges and enums are enforced at agent creation and on mutation. A graph that used to load with an out-of-range value now fails with `3003 GraphCompilationFailed`, and an out-of-range `ChangeAgentParam` returns `3007 InvalidParamValue`. `sampling.max_tokens` is fixed at creation (`3006 ParamNotMutable`). It defaults to 758 and must be at least 1 and less than the node's context size. A failed `string_storage` or retrieve/classify filter rebind returns `3007` and leaves the previous value in force. `threshold` on `Retrieve` and `ClassifyIntent` accepts a cosine distance up to 2.
- **`ClassifyIntentLLM.system_prompt` must reference `{{intents_block}}`.** An empty, unparsable or incomplete template now fails `CreateAgent` and `ChangeAgentParam`. Its parameter order also changed (`system_prompt`, `intents_ids`, `intents_prompt`, `intents`). Unity and Unreal assets load by name and are unaffected.
- **Intent payloads no longer carry the agent id.** Unity `TryllClient.IntentClassified` and `IntentLlmClassified` are now `Action<ulong, T>`, called with `(agentId, classification)`, which matches Unreal's session delegates. `AgentId` is removed from `TryllIntentClassification`, `TryllIntentLlmClassification`, `FTryllIntentClassification` and `FTryllIntentLlmClassification`.
- **The storage folder is process-wide.** `CreateSession` no longer takes a storage data folder, and relative paths resolve against the server's storage root. Unity and Unreal default to `<Project>/TryllStorage/`, and a storage path under `Assets/` or `Content/` is rejected. Move existing storage content there. See [Ship storage folders for builds](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/ship-storage-folders-for-builds.html).
- **Config and CLI removals, with no aliases.** `models_download_dir` is replaced by `models_root`. `crash_dump.dir` and `--crash-dump-dir` are gone, and crash dumps always use the logs folder (`logs_dir` / `--log-dir`). `log_mode` no longer chooses the log file name. The committed `server-config.json` sets no root keys.
- **`local_path` must be inside the storage root.** A catalog `variants[].local_path` that resolves outside the process storage root is ignored with a warning, so the old `C:/models`-style example no longer loads. Use a relative path such as `"LocalModels"`. Client Prod ignores `local_path` entirely. Every variant of a model must now name the same engine.
- **Runtime model helpers removed.** Unreal `UTryllSubsystem::RequestModel` and `OnModelReady` are removed. Replace them with the explicit download / load sequence under [Models and catalogs](#models-and-catalogs); Blueprint graphs need the node and event replaced by hand. Unity `TryllClient.RequestDeleteModel` / `DeleteModelComplete` are no longer public, so delete downloaded files from **Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Model Manager**.
- **Unreal `TryllVoiceInputComponent.bWaitForAgentReady` is removed.** Voice input is now created as soon as the session is ready. If you relied on the delay, set `bCreateOnConnect` to false and call `CreateVoiceInput()` from the agent's `OnAgentReady`.
- **A dialog snapshot written after a fold cannot be imported by an older server.** It fails there with `3022 DialogUnsupportedComponent`. Snapshots from agents that never summarized are unaffected, and this release reads every older snapshot.
- **A broken `models.json` stops the server** instead of starting with an empty catalog.

## New error codes

- **`4106 HotwordBiasDisabled`** — a voice input supplied a hotwords lexicon for a model on which this session turned hotword biasing off.
- **`4107 InvalidHotwordsScore`** — `hotwords_score` is not a finite, non-negative number.
- **`6009 ModelManagementDisabled`** — `DownloadModel` or `DeleteModel` in a deployment mode that does not manage models (Client Prod). Ship every model with the game.
- **`8101 StorageBusy`** — a mutable-KB export, import, save or load was refused because an agent is not strictly idle.
- **`8102 SchemaMismatch`** — the store already exists under a different schema.
- **`8103 MaxRecordsExceeded`** — the schema's `max_records` cap is reached.
- **`8104 UnknownSchema`** — the schema name is not in `schemas.json`, or that file failed to load.
- **`8105 MutableKbSnapshotInvalid`** — the `TMKB` snapshot is malformed, missing fields, or has an unsupported format version.
- **`8106 StorageSnapshotTooLarge`** — a store or game-memory snapshot exceeds its size cap.
- **`8107 InvalidEmbedTiming`** — `LoadGameMemory` was called without `Now` or `Lazy`.
- **`8108 UnknownMutableKb`** — the named store does not exist. Call `EnsureMutableKb` first.
- **`8109 SavesDisabled`** — `SaveGameMemory` / `SaveDialog` refused because saves are disabled for this process. Loads still work.

See [Error Codes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html) for the full list.

# v0.9.0

This release gives every character **its own voice**. The voice moves off the speaking nodes and onto the agent as one **voice profile**. One workflow can then serve a whole cast, and game code can switch a character's **delivery mode** (angry, calm, whisper) mid-turn. LLM nodes can now load **LoRA adapters**, a new **`ClassifyAttributesLLM`** node scores several traits of a line in one call, and prompts can be **localized through your game's own string tables**. **Qwen3-TTS** clones a voice in ten languages, and new **Use Cases** and **Model Benchmarks** sections help you choose a design and a model.

The voice move, the classifier changes and the LoRA field all change the schema, and existing workflows need manual migration. See [Breaking changes and behavior changes](#breaking-changes-and-behavior-changes) and [Migrate to the agent voice](#migrate-to-the-agent-voice) **before** upgrading the plugin.

## Highlights

- **One voice per agent.** A [voice profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html) holds the TTS model, the speaker or reference clip, speed, language, lip sync and named delivery modes. Every speaking node of the agent uses it, so one workflow can drive many characters, each with its own voice. See [Add voice output to an agent](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/add-voice-to-an-agent.html).
- **Delivery modes.** Define moods such as `angry`, `calm` or `whisper` on a profile and switch between them from game code at any time, even mid-turn. The new mode applies from the next sentence. See [Delivery modes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html#delivery-modes).
- **LoRA adapters on LLM nodes.** Load a GGUF LoRA adapter trained for the node's model, with a scale, on any generating or classifying node. A small adapter can teach a small model a narrow job. See [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html).
- **Score several traits in one call.** [`ClassifyAttributesLLM`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-attributes-llm.html) asks up to 16 specialist questions about a line in one batched call, with choice, true/false and 0–1 score answers written to slots.
- **Localized prompts from your string tables.** Tick **Localized** on a prompt and Unity or Unreal resolves it through your own localization system before the agent is created. A language change updates live agents. See [Localize prompts with your localization system](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/localize-prompts.html).
- **Qwen3-TTS.** Voice cloning from a 3–10 s reference clip, in 10 languages, on the same GPU backends as the language models. See [TTS models](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/tts-models.html).
- **Use Cases and Model Benchmarks.** New docs sections that start from what the player experiences ([Use Cases](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/use-cases/index.html)) and from how catalog models perform on Tryll's own jobs ([Model Benchmarks](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/model-benchmarks/index.html)).

## Agent voice

- **Voice profiles.** A `VoiceProfile` holds the TTS model (`tts_model_name`, now required), the base identity (`speaker_id`, `reference_voice` or `voice_description`), `speed`, `lang`, `emit_visemes` and named delivery modes. Unity has a **Voice Profile** asset (**Create → Tryll → Voice Profile**) assigned to the **Voice** field of `TryllAgentComponent`. Unreal has a **Tryll Voice Profile** data asset assigned to the agent component's **Voice Profile**. Python passes `create_agent(graph, voice=...)`, and C++ sets `AgentCreateOptions::voice`. See [Voice Profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html), [TryllVoiceProfile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-voice-profile.html) and the [Blueprint catalog](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unreal/blueprint-catalog.html).
- **Delivery modes.** A profile defines named moods. Switch with `set_delivery_mode` (Python), `SetDeliveryMode` (C++), `SetDeliveryModeAsync` (Unity) or **Set Delivery Mode** (Unreal), with an optional 0–1 intensity. `neutral` is built in. What a mode can change depends on the model: a reference clip (Pocket TTS, Qwen3-TTS), a delivery clause with a low/medium/high intensity word (Maya1), or only speed (Supertonic 3). Orpheus modes must be empty. See [Delivery modes by family](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/tts-models.html#delivery-modes-by-family) and [Clone a voice](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/clone-a-voice.html), where "one clip per mood" is now one delivery mode per mood.
- **Per-agent delivery override.** Unity `TryllAgentComponent` (`OverrideVoiceDelivery` / `VoiceDelivery`) and Unreal `UTryllAgentComponent` (**Voice Delivery**) can start one agent in a different mode without editing the shared profile asset. Changing it also switches a live agent in Play or in Chat.
- **Change the voice at runtime.** `set_voice` / `SetVoice` / `SetVoiceAsync` / **Set Voice** replace the whole profile, model included, while the agent is idle. The new profile is checked and its clips are prepared before the swap, and if anything fails the old voice stays. The active mode is kept when the new profile defines it. Otherwise the new profile's default mode applies, and the acknowledgement carries a warning. See [Change the voice or its delivery at runtime](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/add-voice-to-an-agent.html#8-change-the-voice-or-its-delivery-at-runtime).
- **The voice is checked once, when it is set.** A field the model cannot use fails with `3023 InvalidVoiceProfile` and names the field. A missing TTS model is now `3023`. A non-empty `lang` on a fixed-language voice (Pocket TTS, Orpheus, Maya1) is now rejected instead of silently ignored.
- **Clips are prepared up front.** By default every reference clip in a profile, including each mode's clip, is prepared when the voice is set, so switching mood adds no delay. Set `prepare` to `Lazy` to prepare each clip on first use. See [Clip preparation](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html#clip-preparation).
- **`Speak` nodes emit visemes.** `emit_visemes` is on the voice, so every speaking node of a lip-synced character sends a viseme track, including `Speak` lines such as scripted refusals.
- **One audio stream per turn.** The audio format is announced once per turn, by the first speaking node, and viseme offsets count from it across every speaking node of the turn. See [Audio stream per turn](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html#audio-stream-per-turn).
- **Agents that never speak load no TTS model**, even if they have a voice.
- **Model capabilities drive the editors.** `ListModels` reports `expressiveness` and `num_speakers` for TTS models, and every shipped TTS model declares its capabilities. The Unity and Unreal profile editors show only the fields the chosen model accepts. See [Model Management](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/model-management.html).
- **Maya1 delivery keywords match whole words.** `unhappy` no longer resolves to the `happy` clause.
- **Diagnostics show the agent's voice.** It appears under `tts` on `GenerateAndSpeak` and under a new `voice` section on `Speak`, with `delivery_mode` and `intensity`. The old `tts_lang` / `tts_voice` keys are now `lang` / `reference_voice`. See [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html).

### Migrate to the agent voice

No migration helper ships. Unity drops the removed node fields from a workflow asset the next time it is saved, and Unreal drops them when an old asset loads. So **record the values first**.

**Before upgrading the plugin**, write down the TTS values of every `Speak` or `GenerateAndSpeak` node in every workflow asset: **Tts Model Name**, **Speaker Id**, **Speed**, **Tts Lang**, **Tts Voice**, **Tts Voice Description**, **Tts Delivery Instruction** and **Emit Visemes**. Also note any game code that sets these fields on node params (for example a per-character speaker or speed) or changes them with `ChangeParams` / `ChangeAgentParam`.

**Unity projects**, after upgrading:

1. Create one voice profile per character: **Create → Tryll → Voice Profile**.
1. Fill it from your notes: **Tts Model Name**, **Speaker Id**, **Speed**, **Lang** (was Tts Lang), **Reference Voice** (was Tts Voice), **Voice Description** and **Emit Visemes**. **Tts Model Name** is now required. A node that left it empty used the first TTS model in the catalog, usually `Supertonic 3 (int8)`. Turn a **Tts Delivery Instruction** into a delivery mode with that **Instruction**, and select it from code with `SetDeliveryModeAsync`.
1. Assign the profile to the **Voice** field of each `TryllAgentComponent` whose workflow speaks. For characters spawned at runtime, set `TryllAgentComponent.Voice` before the agent is created. Replace code that patched `SpeakerId` / `Speed` into cloned node params with one profile per character.
1. Re-save each workflow asset so it no longer carries the removed fields.
1. Replace runtime voice changes made with `ChangeParams` by `SetVoiceAsync` (identity) or `SetDeliveryModeAsync` (mood).

**Unreal projects**, after upgrading:

1. Create one **Tryll Voice Profile** data asset per character and fill it from your notes, as for Unity. Check **Emit Visemes** for characters with lip sync. It now also covers `Speak` nodes, so lines from a `Speak` node move the lips too.
1. Assign the profile to the **Voice Profile** property of each `UTryllAgentComponent` whose workflow speaks.
1. Open and re-save each workflow asset, and recompile Blueprints that read or set TTS fields on node params. They must not touch a removed field.
1. Replace runtime voice changes made with **Change Params** by **Set Voice** (identity) or **Set Delivery Mode** (mood).

**Python and C++ code:**

1. Move the `tts_*` fields, `speaker_id`, `speed` and `emit_visemes` off `SpeakParams` / `GenerateAndSpeakParams` into a `VoiceProfile`. `tts_lang` becomes `lang`, `tts_voice` becomes `reference_voice`, `tts_voice_description` becomes `voice_description`, and `tts_delivery_instruction` becomes a `DeliveryMode` with that `instruction`.
1. Pass it at creation: `client.create_agent(graph, voice=profile)` in Python, `AgentCreateOptions::voice` in C++.
1. Replace `change_param` / `ChangeParams` calls on voice fields with `set_voice` / `SetVoice` or `set_delivery_mode` / `SetDeliveryMode`.

If two speaking nodes in one workflow had different voice settings, choose one. An agent now has exactly one voice.

## LoRA adapters

- **An `adaptation` table on every LLM node.** `Generate`, `ToolCall`, `ClassifyIntentLLM`, `ClassifyAttributesLLM`, `GenerateAndSpeak` and `Summarize` take a list of GGUF LoRA adapters (`loras`), each with a scale (`1` = as trained, `0` = off), up to 8 per node. Paths are relative to the storage root, like voice clips. An escaping path fails with `3009 StorageOutsideRoot`, and a missing file with `3010 StorageFileNotFound`. See [Generate](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/generate.html).
- **An adapter must be trained for the node's model.** A file made for another model fails agent creation.
- **Adapters are fixed at creation.** Changing `adaptation` on a live agent returns `3006 ParamNotMutable`. Workflows without it run on the base model as before.
- **Unity has a file picker for adapter paths,** and the workflow validator flags an absolute or `..` path as an error and a missing or non-`.gguf` file as a warning.

## Classification

- **New [`ClassifyAttributesLLM`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-attributes-llm.html) node.** One node scores up to 16 specialist prompts in one cached, batched call. A **Choice** attribute writes a label and can trigger per option. A **Boolean** attribute writes `true` / `false` for one statement. A **Score** attribute writes a normalised 0–1 level. Any trigger takes `triggered_exit`, otherwise the node takes `default_exit`. A Choice that misses `threshold` or `margin` writes `uncertain_choice`, which is one of its choice ids or the reserved `#uncertain`. Empty input never triggers. Engine failure follows `on_failure`. Slots are named `<output_name>_<attribute>`, and `notify_client` emits `attributes_classified` with every measurement. Python, C++, Unity and Unreal all support it, including the editor palettes, inspectors and Dialog Lab attribute checks.
- **`ClassifyIntentLLM` writes its decision to a slot.** New `output_name` (empty = node name). The slot holds the winning id on `found` and `not_found_intent` on every `not_found` path, so a `Branch` can route on it after either exit. `not_found_intent` also accepts the reserved `#uncertain`. See [Output slot](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-intent-llm.html#output-slot).
- **`intents` is the only intent list.** The comma-separated `intents_ids` / `intents_prompt` pair deprecated in [v0.8.0](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/release-notes/v0.8.0.html#intent-classification) is removed (see [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes-and-behavior-changes)).

## Localization

- **Localized prompts use your string tables.** Tick **Localized** on a prompt field and the box becomes a Text ID. Before the agent is created, Unity or Unreal asks your text provider for the text and sends it. See [Localize prompts with your localization system](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/localize-prompts.html).
- **A language change updates live agents.** Ticked non-structural prompts (system prompt, template, instruction, acknowledge text) are updated from the next turn, and params you changed at runtime are kept. The update is all or nothing per agent. If a Text ID is missing in the new language, that agent's prompts stay as they were and `LocalizedTextFailed` (Unity) / `OnLocalizedTextFailed` (Unreal) fires. ClassifyIntent entry prompts, files already bound and an open voice input still need the agent recreated or the input reopened. See [Ship an agent in another language](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/ship-in-another-language.html).
- **Unreal: wait for the new text.** `OnLocalizedTextApplied` fires once an agent's new prompts are acknowledged, so a prefill or reset can wait for them. A server rejection of the update now also raises `OnLocalizedTextFailed`. The Unreal text provider is **None** by default, so existing projects keep using the Tryll **Locale** field.

## Models and catalogs

- **Qwen3-TTS 12Hz 1.7B Base (Q4_K_M)** is a public catalog voice. It clones its voice from a reference clip, so the profile's `reference_voice` is required. It speaks zh, en, de, it, pt, es, ja, ko, fr and ru through `lang`, and it runs on the CPU, Vulkan and CUDA backends without ONNX Runtime. Delivery modes switch reference clips. See [TTS models](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/tts-models.html).
- **SenseVoice Multilingual** and **Streaming Paraformer zh-en** are now public speech-to-text entries.
- **LFM2.5 1.2B Thinking (Q4_K_M)** joins the catalog. It always opens with a `<think>` block, so it is not a good host for an immersion guard.
- **New [Model Benchmarks](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/model-benchmarks/index.html) section.** Model cards and per-trait leaderboards for catalog models: the immersion guard (General and World classifiers), prefill and generation speed for a 1K and a 4K prompt, and VRAM at an 8K context. Treat the results as provisional.

## Diagnostics and Agent Log

- **Prefill and generation speed per node.** Language-model nodes add `engine.llama_perf` to turn diagnostics, with prompt and generation time and token counts for the node's context. See [Turn Diagnostics JSON](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/turn-diagnostics-json.html).
- **Agent Log export.** **Export** writes the journal to one JSON file in Unity and Unreal. The file has a header describing the server, the capture and the agents, then the events with their payloads, then a turn index. The inspectors show the event's raw JSON. The file can contain player input, prompts and tool arguments, so treat it like a bug report. See [Use the Agent Log](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/use-agent-log.html) and [Agent Log format](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/agent-log-format.html).

## Unreal

- **Play → Standalone Game starts its own server.** A standalone game used to skip auto-launch silently and then fail every connect attempt. It now launches the bundled server on a free port, separate from the editor's server, and the server exits 60 s after the game closes. See [Auto-launch the server](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/auto-launch-server.html).
- **Saved assets survive node parameter changes.** Workflow and agent assets saved by an older plugin load correctly after a node field is removed, renamed or given a new default. A saved `ClassifyIntentLLM` CSV intent pair is converted into `intents` on load.

## Documentation

- **New [Use Cases](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/use-cases/index.html) section.** Each page starts from what the player experiences and lists the building blocks that produce it, with links to the how-to guides: [Talking NPC](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/use-cases/talking-npc.html) step by step, [Ambient world](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/use-cases/ambient-world.html), [Voice control](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/use-cases/voice-control.html), [In-game assistant](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/use-cases/in-game-assistant.html), and [AI director](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/use-cases/ai-director.html), an idea we have not built yet.
- **New reference pages:** [Voice Profile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/voice-profile.html), [TryllVoiceProfile](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-voice-profile.html), [Classify Attributes (LLM)](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/nodes/classify-attributes-llm.html) and [Agent Log format](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/agent-log-format.html). [TTS models](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/tts-models.html) gains a per-family table of what a delivery mode can change.

## Breaking changes and behavior changes

- **The schema changed — rebuild every client.** The agent voice, `ClassifyAttributesLLM`, the `ClassifyIntentLLM` changes and LoRA adapters all change shape. **Upgrade the server and every client together** (Unity, Unreal, Python, C++). An older server would ignore `adaptation` and quietly run the base model, so mismatched peers fail at connect: the client rejects the server's protocol version with `5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch`. See [Wire Protocol](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html#versioning).
- **One voice per agent.** `Speak` and `GenerateAndSpeak` lose `tts_model_name`, `speaker_id`, `speed`, `tts_lang`, `tts_voice`, `tts_voice_description`, `tts_delivery_instruction` and `emit_visemes`. They keep only their text routing and chunking (`min_sentence_chars`, `first_chunk_max_chars`). A graph with a speaking node and no voice fails with `3025 AgentVoiceRequired`. An agent created without a voice cannot be given one later. `ChangeAgentParam` can no longer change any voice field. Write down your TTS values **before** you upgrade the plugin, then follow [Migrate to the agent voice](#migrate-to-the-agent-voice).
- **`tts_model_name` is required.** An empty name no longer means "the first TTS voice in the catalog", and a missing TTS model fails with `3023 InvalidVoiceProfile` instead of `3003 GraphCompilationFailed`.
- **Fixed-language voices reject `lang`.** A non-empty `lang` on Pocket TTS, Orpheus or Maya1 fails with `3023` instead of being ignored. Leave it empty.
- **The audio format is announced once per turn.** A turn with two speaking nodes no longer sends a second format frame or restarts the viseme clock. Code that reset playback on each format announcement now sees one per turn.
- **`ClassifyIntentLLM` CSV intents removed.** `intents_ids` / `intents_prompt` are gone, and `intents` (id + prompt pairs) must hold 2–26 entries. Unreal assets convert a saved CSV pair on load. If the two lists had different lengths, the missing entries are left empty and a warning is logged. Other assets that still carry a CSV pair must move it to `intents` before upgrading. The diagnostics key `parameters.intents_ids` is unchanged.
- **LoRA adapters are structural.** `adaptation` is fixed at agent creation. Changing it on a live agent returns `3006 ParamNotMutable`.
- **Unreal Play → Standalone Game launches a server.** A standalone run that used to have no server now starts its own on a free port.

## New error codes

- **`3023 InvalidVoiceProfile`** — a voice profile field fails validation, names an unknown model, or uses a field the model cannot use.
- **`3024 UnknownDeliveryMode`** — `SetAgentDeliveryMode` named a mode the voice does not define. The current mode stays.
- **`3025 AgentVoiceRequired`** — a speaking graph has no voice, or a voice call was made on an agent created without one.

See [Error Codes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html) for the full list.
# Model Benchmarks

# Model Benchmarks

Provisional · immersion guard, speed and memory

How catalog models do on the jobs Tryll gives them, measured by the Tryll team on our own test sets. Measured so far: the immersion guard, General guard (attempts to pull the NPC out of the game) and World guard (lines that do not belong in the setting), and speed and memory: how fast a model reads its prompt and writes its answer, and how much graphics memory it needs. NPC roleplay, tool calling and summarization will follow.

*The numbers are provisional: 13 models. The guard is measured once per model (it reads probabilities and does not sample), at a 5 in 100 false-block budget, with World guard on one game setting. Speed and memory are measured on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti with Vulkan; other hardware gives other numbers.*

# General guard

setting-invariant classifier

The share of attempts to pull the NPC out of the game that the guard blocks: asking whether it is an AI, jailbreaks, prompt leaks, coding requests and format tricks. Each model's threshold is set so that at most 5 in 100 normal player lines are blocked on a tuning set; the numbers here are on separate, held-out lines.

# VRAM at 8K context

one agent, 8K context, q8_0 KV cache

Graphics memory one agent needs, as llama.cpp reports it: the model weights, the KV cache for an 8,192-token context stored as q8_0, and the compute buffers. Every extra agent on the same model adds its own KV cache and compute buffers; the weights are shared.

## VRAM at 8K context

## Measured models

| Model                                 | VRAM    | Weights | KV cache | Compute | Rank      | Family    |
| ------------------------------------- | ------- | ------- | -------- | ------- | --------- | --------- |
| Bonsai 8B (Q1_0 1-bit)                | 1.90 GB | 1.15 GB | 0.64 GB  | 0.10 GB | #1 of 13  | Bonsai    |
| SmolLM2 1.7B Instruct (Q4_K_M)        | 1.98 GB | 1.05 GB | 0.86 GB  | 0.07 GB | #2 of 13  | SmolLM2   |
| Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)        | 2.58 GB | 2.01 GB | 0.50 GB  | 0.07 GB | #3 of 13  | Llama     |
| Ministral 3 3B Instruct (Q4_K_M)      | 2.69 GB | 2.14 GB | 0.46 GB  | 0.09 GB | #4 of 13  | Ministral |

# World guard

measured on 1 setting

The share of lines that do not belong in the game world that the guard blocks, at the same 5 in 100 budget. Measured on one setting, a medieval merchant, so treat it as a first signal rather than a promise for every world.

# Bonsai 8B (Q1_0 1-bit)

Model card

**As an immersion guard, blocks 32 in 100 general attacks and 60 in 100 world attacks at a 5% false-block budget. Writes 238 tokens per second and needs 1.9 GB of VRAM at 8K context.**

Bonsai · 8B · Q1_0 1-bit · 1.2 GB file · prism-ml/Bonsai-8B-gguf

Measured 2026-10-07 · Tryll 0.8.0-DEV · llama.cpp b10839 · NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti · vulkan · one deterministic pass (classifiers do not sample) · speed: median of 10 runs · ranked against 13 models

## Plain words

*What the measured numbers mean for a game. Intervals and ranks are under In the field.*

**32 in 100** · Classification · General guard. Blocks 32 in 100 attempts to pull the NPC out of the game: asking whether it is an AI, jailbreaks, prompt leaks, coding requests and format tricks. *Normal player lines wrongly blocked: 5 in 100 on held-out lines (the budget is 5 in 100, set on a separate tuning set).*

**60 in 100** · Classification · World guard. Blocks 60 in 100 lines that do not belong in the setting, such as paying by phone in a medieval town or asking how long chicken keeps in the fridge. *Normal player lines wrongly blocked: 3 in 100 on held-out lines (the budget is 5 in 100, set on a separate tuning set).*

*World guard is measured on one setting, a medieval merchant. A different world needs its own check.*

**4,805 tokens/s** · Performance · Prefill. Reads a 3,959-token prompt in 0.82 s. The first token reaches the player after 0.85 s. *A 1,146-token prompt: first token after 0.26 s.*

**238 tokens/s** · Performance · Generation. Writes 238 tokens per second after a 1K-token prompt, and 217 after a 4K-token prompt. *200 tokens take 0.8 s.*

**1.9 GB VRAM** · Performance · Memory. Weights 1.15 GB, KV cache 0.64 GB for 8,192 tokens (q8_0), compute buffers 0.10 GB. *Each extra agent on this model adds its own KV cache and compute buffers; the weights are shared.*

*Speed and memory were measured on one GPU, named in the header. Other hardware gives other numbers.*

### Not measured yet

- **NPC roleplay**: clean speech, staying in lore and role, writing quality
- **Tool calling**: call accuracy and restraint
- **Summarization**: how long the summary keeps what the player said
- **Intent classification**: the butler set is too small for a card number

## In the field

*Where this model sits among the measured models. Right is better. The blue bar is the 95% interval. Guard ranks come from paired comparisons; a speed rank is above another only when the two intervals do not overlap. Close models share a range.*

**World guard** · #8–12 of 13 · *measured on 1 setting*

# Unity Client API

**Package:** `com.tryll.client`\
**Namespace:** `Tryll.Client`\
**Target:** Unity 6 (6000.x), .NET Standard 2.1, Windows Standalone + Editor

> The Unity client is a hand-authored C# port of the Unreal plugin. The public surface is documented on this page and the entity pages linked below. Internal types under `Tryll.Client.Internal` are not part of the public API.

## TryllAgent

`IDisposable` handle for a server-side agent. Obtained from `TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync` or from `TryllAgentComponent.Agent`.

```
public ulong AgentId { get; }
public bool  IsValid { get; }

// Actions
public void SendMessage(string text);
public void Cancel(TryllCancelMode mode = TryllCancelMode.StopAndKeep);
public void ChangeParams(string nodeName, TryllNodeParamsBase @params,
                         Action<TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void Resume(string resumeNode = "", Action<TryllError> onComplete = null);
public TryllNodeParamsBase GetNodeParamsBaseline(string nodeName);
public void AppendInteractions(
    IReadOnlyList<TryllDialogInteraction> interactions,
    Action<uint, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void RemoveInteractionsFromEnd(
    int count,
    Action<uint, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void ExportDialog(
    Action<TryllDialogSnapshot, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void ImportDialog(
    TryllDialogSnapshot snapshot,
    TryllDialogCompatibility compatibility = TryllDialogCompatibility.Strict,
    Action<TryllDialogImportResult, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void SaveDialog(string path, string saveId,
                       Action<TryllDialogFileSaveResult, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void LoadDialog(string path,
                       TryllDialogCompatibility compatibility = TryllDialogCompatibility.Strict,
                       Action<TryllDialogFileLoadResult, TryllError> onComplete = null);
public void RegisterTool(string toolName, Func<TryllToolCall, string> handler);
public void RegisterTool(string toolName, Func<TryllToolCall, Task<string>> handler);
public TryllAgentVariables Variables { get; }

// Voice (protocol v27)
public Task<TryllError> SetVoiceAsync(TryllVoiceProfileData voice);
public Task<TryllError> SetVoiceAsync(Tryll.VoiceProfileT voice);
public Task<TryllError> SetDeliveryModeAsync(string mode, float intensity = 1f);

// Delivery callbacks (last-writer-wins; pass null to clear).
// All fire on the Unity main thread. Register before SendMessage.
public void SetOnAnswerText(Action<string, string, bool, bool> callback);
public void SetOnTurnComplete(Action<TryllTurnStatus, string, int> callback);
public void SetOnError(Action<TryllError> callback);
public void SetOnTtsAudioFormat(Action<string, int, int, int> callback);
public void SetOnTtsAudio(Action<string, ArraySegment<short>> callback);
// Lip-sync track (voice profile with EmitVisemes). Additive multicast (+=);
// the array is valid only during the callback — copy it to keep it.
public event Action<string, TryllVisemeEvent[]> OnTtsVisemes;
public event Action<TryllError> ToolHandlerError;

// Lifetime
public void Dispose();
```

A code-created agent (`RequestCreateAgentAsync` without a component) must register `SetOnAnswerText` / `SetOnTurnComplete` before `SendMessage` or the reply is discarded. Pass `null` to clear. These replace any previously set callback (not multicast). `ToolHandlerError` is a separate multicast event for `RegisterTool` handler / resume failures.

`ChangeParams` / `onComplete` and `Resume` / `onComplete` deliver a [`TryllError`](#tryllerror) value — check `error.IsOk` (it is a struct; success is not null). `GetNodeParamsBaseline` returns a deep copy (or `null` if unknown). `ChangeParams` is allowed while idle **or paused**.

`SetVoiceAsync` replaces the agent's [voice](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-voice-profile.html); it is admitted while idle or paused (`AgentBusy` otherwise) and keeps the old voice when the new one is rejected (`InvalidVoiceProfile`). `SetDeliveryModeAsync` switches the delivery mode at any time, from the next sentence (`UnknownDeliveryMode`, or `AgentVoiceRequired` when the agent has no voice). Both return the server's verdict as a `TryllError`.

`Variables` is the agent's typed [Agent Variables](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/agent-variables.html) mirror — see [`TryllAgentVariables`](#tryllagentvariables) below.

For Inspector-friendly wrappers with `OnParamChanged` / `OnResumed` UnityEvents, prefer [`TryllAgentComponent`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-agent-component.html).

`AppendInteractions` / `RemoveInteractionsFromEnd` use [`TryllDialogInteraction`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/index.html#trylldialoginteraction) pairs — strict idle-only; see [Seed and edit dialog history](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/seed-and-edit-dialog-history.html).

`ExportDialog` / `ImportDialog` return a [`TryllDialogSnapshot`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/export-and-import-dialog.html) (full-fidelity replace). `ToFlatBufferBytes` / `FromFlatBufferBytes` are the canonical `TDLG` helpers — the game owns the save file. See [Save and Load Agent State](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/save-and-load-agent-state.html) for multi-agent coordination, variable restoration, and save-slot handling.

Ownership

If you obtain a `TryllAgent` directly from `TryllClient.RequestCreateAgentAsync` (not via `TryllAgentComponent`), you own it and **must** call `Dispose()`.

______________________________________________________________________

## Experimental mutable knowledge bases

`TryllClient.EnsureMutableKbAsync(name, schema)` returns a session-bound `TryllMutableKb` handle. `LoadGameMemoryAsync` requires `Now` or `Lazy` — `Unspecified` fails locally with `8107 InvalidEmbedTiming`. Inspect stores in **Window ▸ Tryll ▸ Knowledge** (stores · Filter/Query records · modify).

```
public sealed class TryllMutableKb
{
    public bool IsValid { get; }
    public string Name { get; }
    public string Schema { get; }

    public Task<(List<TryllMutableKbWriteResult> results, TryllError error)> WriteAsync(
        IReadOnlyList<TryllMutableKbUpsert> records);
    public Task<(uint deletedCount, TryllError error)> DeleteAsync(IReadOnlyList<string> ids);
    public Task<(uint clearedCount, TryllError error)> ClearAsync();
    public Task<(List<TryllMutableKbHit> hits, TryllError error)> QueryAsync(
        string queryText, uint topK = 4, RetrievalMode retrievalMode = RetrievalMode.Dense);
    public Task<(TryllMutableKbRecord record, TryllError error)> GetAsync(string id);
    public Task<(TryllMutableKbListPage page, TryllError error)> ListAsync(
        uint offset = 0, uint limit = 50);
    public Task<(TryllMutableKbStats stats, TryllError error)> StatsAsync();
    public Task<(TryllMutableKbSnapshot snapshot, TryllError error)> ExportAsync();
    public Task<(TryllMutableKbImportResult result, TryllError error)> ImportAsync(
        TryllMutableKbSnapshot snapshot,
        TryllMutableKbCompatibility compatibility = TryllMutableKbCompatibility.Strict);
}
```

`ImportAsync` rejects a snapshot whose `Name` does not match the handle (`8105 MutableKbSnapshotInvalid`) before anything is sent.

```
[Serializable]
public struct TryllDialogInteraction
{
    public string UserMessage;      // empty → omit user side
    public string AssistantMessage; // empty → omit assistant side; both empty → skipped
}
```

## TryllAgentVariables

Typed per-agent [Variables](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/concepts/agent-variables.html) mirror, reachable via the `TryllAgent.Variables` property (e.g. `agentComp.Agent.Variables`).

```
public TryllError SetInt(string name, long value);
public TryllError SetFloat(string name, double value);
public TryllError SetString(string name, string value);
public TryllError SetBool(string name, bool value);
public TryllError SetStringSet(string name, IEnumerable<string> value);
public TryllError AddToSet(string name, string element);
public TryllError RemoveFromSet(string name, string element);
public TryllError Reset(string name);

public long   GetInt(string name);
public double GetFloat(string name);
public string GetString(string name);
public bool   GetBool(string name);
public IReadOnlyList<string> GetStringSet(string name);   // defensive copy
```

Setters validate locally — an unknown name or type mismatch returns a non-`Ok` `TryllError` immediately, with no wire round-trip. Writes update the local mirror synchronously; the actual `UpdateAgentVariablesRequest` is batched and flushed automatically immediately before the agent's next `SendMessage`/`Resume`/`ChangeParams` call.

```
var vars = agentComp.Agent.Variables;
var err = vars.SetInt("level", 13);
if (!err.IsOk) Debug.LogError($"{err.Code}: {err.Message}");
vars.AddToSet("quests_reached", "lost_amulet");
```

Declare variables on [`TryllWorkflowAsset.Variables`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-workflow-asset.html); a component's `VariableOverrides` may override an asset's declared initial value per-instance (Material-Instance pattern — the Inspector shows one optional row per declaration). Play Mode override edits update the live mirror; flush remains deferred (or use **Flush Now** in the Inspector).

______________________________________________________________________

## TryllError

Value-type error struct. Always check `IsOk` before using an API result.

```
[Serializable]
public struct TryllError
{
    public int    Code;        // 0 = OK. See TryllErrorCode enum for named values.
    public string Message;
    public bool   IsOk => Code == 0;
    public static TryllError Ok();
}
```

______________________________________________________________________

## TryllErrorCode

Named error code constants, generated from the server `ErrorCodes.h` into `Runtime/Generated/TryllErrorCode.gen.cs`. See [Error Codes](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/error-codes.html) for the full table.

```
public enum TryllErrorCode
{
    Ok = 0,
    // Connection: 1001–1003
    // Session: 2001–2005 (2004 InvalidLocale, 2005 InvalidEngineSet)
    // Agent: 3001–3022 (3012 AgentNotPaused, 3013–3015 Variables,
    //        3016 InvalidToolResults, 3018–3022 Dialog snapshots)
    // Inference: 4001–4005 (4004–4005 KV cache)
    // VoiceInput / STT: 4100–4107
    // Protocol: 5001–5006 (5004 ProtocolVersionMismatch is raised client-side)
    // Download / models: 6001–6005, 6007–6009
    // StringStorage: 7001–7004
    // EmbeddedStringStorage: 8001–8003
    // Mutable KB: 8101–8109
}
```

______________________________________________________________________

## TryllGraphDescription and related types

```
[Serializable]
public class TryllGraphDescription
{
    public List<TryllNodeDescription> Nodes = new List<TryllNodeDescription>();
    public string                     StartNode;
    public string                     DefaultModelName;

    public TryllGraphDescription Clone();                  // deep copy, params included
    public T FindParams<T>(string nodeName) where T : TryllNodeParamsBase;
    public bool HasNode(string nodeName);
}

[Serializable]
public class TryllNodeDescription
{
    public string               Name;
    public TryllNodeParamsBase  Params;  // typed subclass; exit fields live here
}
```

Wiring between nodes is set as exit fields directly on the typed `Params` object — e.g. `TryllGenerateParams.DefaultExit`, `TryllRegexGuardrailParams.TriggeredExit`. An **empty string** routes to END (the default). See each node type's params class for the full list of exit fields and configuration params.

Tools are not on the node description. A `ToolCall` node carries them on `TryllToolCallParams.Tools` (`TryllToolDefinition[]`, each with `TryllToolParamDefinition` parameters).

Both types are classes, so one graph instance handed to several agents shares its params objects. Call `Clone()` before customising a copy per agent.

______________________________________________________________________

## TryllGraphBuilder

Fluent builder for `TryllGraphDescription`. Typed `AddXxx()` methods accept a typed params object; exit fields are set on that object before calling `AddXxx()`.

```
var graph = new TryllGraphBuilder()
    .AddGenerate("gen", new TryllGenerateParams
    {
        ModelName   = "mymodel",
        // DefaultExit defaults to "" (END)
    })
    .SetStartNode("gen")
    .SetDefaultModelName("mymodel")
    .Build();
```

## TryllModelInfo

```
[Serializable]
public struct TryllModelInfo
{
    public string                 Name;
    public TryllModelStatus       Status;
    public string                 HuggingFaceRepo;
    public long                   SizeBytes;
    public string                 ModelType;        // "language" | "embedding" | "stt" | "tts" | "vad"
    public string                 Engine;           // catalog engine, e.g. "llama-cpp", "sherpa-onnx"
    public string                 Audience;         // "public" | "experimental" | "internal" | ""
    public string[]               Languages;        // BCP-47 primary subtags; empty = undeclared
    public string                 ToolCallFormat;   // "chatml" | "llama3" | "mistral" | "generic" | ""
    public string                 ToolCallSupport;  // "supported" | "unsupported" | ""
    public int                    ContextSize;      // 0 = engine default
    public string[]               Files;
    public string                 LocalPath;        // empty when not on disk
    public bool                   HasDefaultSampling;
    public TryllSamplingParams    DefaultSampling;  // valid only when HasDefaultSampling
    public TryllModelDependency[] Dependencies;     // shared assets; empty when none
    public bool                   HasTtsCapabilities;
    public TryllTtsCapabilities   TtsCapabilities;  // valid only when HasTtsCapabilities
}

[Serializable]
public struct TryllTtsCapabilities
{
    public bool                  VoiceDescription;     // voice profile VoiceDescription
    public bool                  DeliveryInstruction;  // delivery mode Instruction
    public bool                  ReferenceVoice;       // profile and mode ReferenceVoice
    public bool                  Speed;                // Speed / SpeedScale other than 1.0
    public bool                  LanguagePerCall;      // non-empty Lang
    public bool                  Expressiveness;       // Chatterbox exaggeration
    public int                   NumSpeakers;          // SpeakerId is 0..NumSpeakers-1; 0 = undeclared
    public TryllTtsVoicePreset[] VoicePresets;         // named speakers (Orpheus, Maya1)
    public TryllTtsInlineTag[]   InlineTags;
}
```

`Engine` is read-only catalog data. A model's variants share one engine, and no client call selects it.

## Enumerations

```
public enum TryllInferenceEngine : byte { Mock, LlamaCpp, OnnxGenAI, WindowsML, OpenVino, TensorRtLlm, SherpaOnnx, OnnxRuntime }
public enum TryllNodeType        : byte { Generate, RegexGuardrail, CannedResponse, ToolCall, Retrieve, Instruction, ClassifyIntent, IntentToInstruction, ClassifyIntentLLM, GenerateAndSpeak, Speak, Pause, Transform, Branch, WriteToMemory, Summarize }
public enum TryllTurnStatus      : byte { Success, Error, Cancelled, PauseTimedOut }
public enum TryllCancelMode      : byte { StopAndKeep, StopAndDiscard }
public enum TryllModelStatus     : byte { Absent, Local, Downloading, Loaded, Downloaded, Incomplete }
public enum TryllPlacement       : byte { BeforeUserAsUser, BeforeUserAsSystem, AfterUserAsUser, AfterUserAsSystem }
public enum TryllSendAnswer      : byte { None, Whole, Streamed }
public enum TryllHistoryRole     : byte { None, Assistant }

// Namespace Tryll (not Tryll.Client) — add `using Tryll;`.
public enum WireViseme : byte { sil, PP, FF, TH, DD, kk, CH, SS, nn, RR, aa, E, ih, oh, ou }
```

`TryllNodeType` is 0-based, while the wire `NodeParams` union tag is 1-based. Use the named value, never a raw number. The per-node option enums (`TryllToolCallMode`, `TryllToolCallDisposition`, `TryllRetrievalMode`, `TryllBranchTest`, and the rest) live in `TryllGraphDescription.cs` next to these.

______________________________________________________________________

## Threading and error handling summary

- All events and `Task<T>` completions fire on the Unity **main thread**.
- Always check `error.IsOk` before using any `Task<T>` result.
- Call `TryllAgentComponent.SendMessage` / `CreateAgent` from the main thread only.
- Use `await` only from `async void` methods rooted on the main thread (e.g., `async void Start()`).

# TryllClient

**Type:** `MonoBehaviour` (singleton)\
**Namespace:** `Tryll.Client`\
**Source:** `Runtime/TryllClient.cs`

Singleton `MonoBehaviour` that manages the TCP session to the Tryll server. Created automatically at game start by `TryllClientModule` via `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod(BeforeSceneLoad)]` — you do not add it to a scene yourself.

In Play mode it lives on a `DontDestroyOnLoad` GameObject. In the Editor outside Play mode the static helper `EnsureEditorInstance()` creates a hidden `HideAndDontSave` instance.

______________________________________________________________________

## Connection settings

These are read from [`TryllRuntimeSettings`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-runtime-settings.html) on `Awake`.

| Field        | Type     | Default       |
| ------------ | -------- | ------------- |
| `ServerHost` | `string` | `"127.0.0.1"` |
| `ServerPort` | `int`    | `9100`        |

`RequestGetMemoryConsumptionAsync` is session-scoped (needs `CreateSession`) but the snapshot is **server-wide** — every session on that process. It never fails with `AgentBusy`. See [Inspect Server Memory](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/how-to/inspect-server-memory.html).

______________________________________________________________________

## GPU throttling and background agents

`SetInferenceThrottle` tells the server how hard to yield the GPU back to your game — `0f` = full speed (the default for a session that never calls it), `1f` = maximum yielding. It is fire-and-forget: no request id, no response, nothing to await, so calling it from `Update()` is fine. It never changes what is generated, only how fast.

```
void Update()
{
    // Example policy: yield harder as your own frame time worsens.
    float pressure = Mathf.InverseLerp(11f, 20f, Time.smoothDeltaTime * 1000f);
    TryllClient.Instance.SetInferenceThrottle(pressure);
}
```

Agents nobody is waiting on should say so, so their inference is the first to give way:

```
var (agent, error) = await TryllClient.Instance.RequestCreateAgentAsync(
    graph, workload: Tryll.AgentWorkload.Background);
```

Everything else the server classifies from the graph itself, per turn — streamed `Generate` text is protected, spoken and buffered work absorbs the slack. See [Wire Protocol](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/wire-protocol.html#inference-throttle-and-agent-workload) and [Server configuration](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/server-configuration.html#inference-scheduler).

______________________________________________________________________

## Lifecycle

1. `TryllClientModule` creates the singleton at `BeforeSceneLoad`.
1. `Awake` reads `TryllRuntimeSettings` and applies `ServerHost` / `ServerPort`.
1. Call `Connect()` to open the TCP session (or enable **Auto Launch Server** in settings).
1. Call `CreateSession(...)` to open the session. It may pass an optional engine warm-up hint; it does not choose an engine. Each model's engine comes from its catalog entry.
1. Use `RequestCreateAgentAsync` or attach a [`TryllAgentComponent`](https://docs.tryllengine.com/v0.9/reference/client-api/unity/tryll-agent-component.html).
1. Call `Disconnect()` when done, or let `OnDestroy` clean up on exit.
